title: Controls Technician I
description:
About Us

Amarr, a part of ASSA ABLOY, the global leaders in opening solutions, is a performance driven manufacturing organization committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence. As an industry leader, we empower our teams to innovate, continuously improve, and deliver world class solutions to our customers.

The Controls Technician I is responsible for supporting safe, reliable, and efficient manufacturing operations through hands-on troubleshooting, maintenance, and improvement of PLC-controlled equipment and automation systems. This role also focuses on diagnosing and resolving control-related downtime, performing preventative and predictive maintenance, and supporting equipment startups, modifications, and reliability improvements. Working closely with Maintenance, Engineering, Production, and Operations, to help contribute to continuous improvement efforts, equipment upgrades, and adherence to electrical safety and controls standards.

Key Responsibilities

Controls & Electrical Maintenance Support

  • Troubleshoot, maintain, and repair PLC-controlled manufacturing equipment to support safe and reliable production operations.
  • Diagnose and resolve controls-related equipment downtime involving PLCs, HMIs, sensors, VFDs, servos, and safety devices.
  • Perform preventive and predictive maintenance activities on control systems and automation equipment.
  • Support startup, testing, and validation of repaired or modified equipment.
  • Assist with minor programming changes to PLCs and HMIs under the direction of Engineering or Maintenance leadership.

Hands-On Technical Work

  • Perform hands-on investigation and repair directly on manufacturing lines and equipment.
  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, ladder logic, and control documentation.
  • Support installation, modification, and replacement of control panels, devices, and field wiring.
  • Work safely with energized equipment in accordance with company procedures and applicable electrical safety standards.
  • Document repairs, changes, and improvements made to control systems.

Continuous Improvement & Reliability

  • Identify recurring equipment issues and assist with root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Support equipment reliability improvements through automation and controls enhancements.
  • Collaborate with Engineering on equipment upgrades, retrofits, and automation projects.
  • Recommend improvements to control standards, maintenance practices, and spare parts strategies.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Work cross-functionally with Maintenance, Engineering, Production, and Operations teams.
  • Communicate equipment status, downtime causes, and repair actions clearly to team members and supervisors.
  • Coordinate with outside vendors and contractors for controls-related service and support as needed.
  • Participate in shift handoffs and maintenance meetings to ensure continuity of operations.

Position Requirements

  • High School Diploma or GED plus an associate degree or technical certification in electronics, instrumentation, or mechatronics. A combination of hands-on experience and education can also be considered.
  • Minimum of 1 – 3 years of experience in electrical or maintenance roles.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing processes.
  • Experience with motion control systems, VFDs, and servo drives.
  • Intermediate proficiency with computers and engineering-related software.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills; comfortable working with individuals at all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to work flexible hours as required to support production and project needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical, Controls, or Automation Engineering, or equivalent education and experience.
  • Experience working with outside vendors, system integrators, and equipment OEMs.
  • Ability to document controls standards, procedures, and best practices.
  • Ability to travel occasionally.

Other Job Responsibilities and Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift up to 45 lbs. unassisted with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and/or pull materials weighing more than 45 lbs. using team lifting procedures.
  • Ability to stand and/or walk for extended periods (8–12 hours per shift).
  • Ability to safely move throughout the manufacturing floor.
  • Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, climb stairs and/or ladders as required for job tasks.
  • Ability to use hands, wrists, and fingers for handling materials, writing, and computer work.
  • Frequent use of computers, keyboards, tablets, scanners, or handheld devices.
  • Ability to work in a loud, fast-paced industrial environment.
  • Ability to work in hot and cold environmental conditions.

Benefits include Medical/Dental/Vision, Paid Time Off, and a 401k plan (with an automatic 3% company contribution, regardless of your contribution) among others.

Our goal is to be a world-leading company that attracts diverse talent, where all team members feel safe being their true selves and are able to thrive in a work environment that promotes change, innovation, and provides equal access and opportunity.

We are part of a global company, ASSA ABLOY with a diverse range of opportunities, both locally and abroad. We offer a competitive salary, training and the opportunity to develop and enhance your career. We take great pride in the efforts of our team members who create a supportive team environment and make ASSA ABLOY such a great place to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. Amarr is an E-Verify participant.

description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

We are seeking a highly skilled Propulsion Design Engineer to serve as a senior technical contributor within our propulsion team. This role focuses on the design, release, and continual improvement of mechanical components and assemblies for internal combustion and jet propulsion systems on UAV platforms.

As a design engineer, you’ll lead complex CAD efforts, enforce rigorous design standards, and collaborate directly with Responsible Engineers, technicians, machinists, and production teams to ensure our propulsion hardware is functional, manufacturable, and testable. You will be the cornerstone of configuration control, interface discipline, and design-for-execution within the team.

What You'll Do

  • Own the design of propulsion components and subsystems from concept through production release
  • Develop and maintain high-quality CAD models, detailed drawings, and assemblies using Siemens NX with fully applied GD&T
  • Write and enforce propulsion design standards and contribute to company-wide design best practices
  • Collaborate closely with the machine shop, production team, and technicians to support builds, resolve non-conformances, and drive iterative improvements
  • Develop initial work instructions, assembly guidance, and design documentation for repeatability and scalability
  • Ensure designs are practical, manufacturable, and cost-effective, with strong understanding of machining, tolerances, materials, and assembly workflows
  • Apply engineering analysis and judgment (e.g., hand calcs, GFSSP, ANSYS, FEA, REFPROP) to support sizing, load cases, and design validation
  • Support configuration management, BOM control, and change processes using Teamcenter or equivalent PLM
  • Participate in design reviews, interface control working groups, and root cause investigations

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related engineering discipline
  • 7+ years of experience in mechanical design for aerospace, with direct propulsion hardware experience preferred
  • Expert-level proficiency in CAD modeling and drawing creation (NX preferred) and application of GD&T
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with production, machine shop personnel, and technicians to solve real-time hardware issues
  • Familiarity with design for manufacturing, including machining processes, surface modeling, stack-up analysis, and fabrication limitations
  • Hands-on experience developing assembly work instructions, troubleshooting build issues, and implementing hardware-driven design changes
  • Experience with configuration management, PLM systems (Teamcenter), and BOM structure
  • U.S. Citizenship or ability to comply with ITAR requirements; Ability to obtain Secret clearance

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with GFSSP, REFPROP, ANSYS, FEA, or other mechanical and thermal analysis tools
  • Ability to write Python scripts for design automation, data analysis, or simulation support
  • Proficient in interface control and tolerance stack-up analysis for complex assemblies
  • Knowledge of fastening methods and joint design for high-vibration, aerospace environments
  • Familiarity with high-temperature materials and design practices for thermally stressed components
  • Prior experience designing hardware for internal combustion, turbine, or rocket propulsion systems, particularly in development or test environments
  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related engineering discipline

Reports to: General Manager

Salary Range: $95,000 – $98,000 plus monthly and quarterly incentive

SUMMARY

Responsible for implementing and directing the day-to-day process control and operational activities, plans, and programs to ensure efficient operation of Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) compliance for Pratt’s Staten Island, NY paper mill. Including review of WWTP data and directing process changes to ensure compliance with all applicable permits.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Review WWTP data and directing process changes as needed to ensure compliance with all applicable permits and regulations.
  • Prepare operational reports, statistical reports, trends, graphics, and other data analysis as needed
  • Maintain and submit wastewater compliance records and reports as required by permits
  • Troubleshoot, diagnose, and solve issues related to the operation of the WWTP
  • Schedule, monitor, and interpret required laboratory sample analysis for the Mill’s wastewater permits
  • Ensure all required compliance testing is completed with the proper frequencies, test protocols, holding times, etc.
  • Research and develop continuous improvement projects to improve the Mills’ wastewater operations, cost structure, etc. including planning, scheduling, and executing WWTP outages for equipment and control systems while minimizing impact to Mill production
  • Develop a maintenance plan, spare parts inventory, and critical equipment policy
  • Develop Standard Operating Procedures for facility’s WWTP
  • Review monthly Discharge Monitoring Reports and other quarterly, semi-annual, and annual reports with Mill’s Responsible Official and Senior Environmental personnel
  • Position manages 3 direct reports
  • Additional duties as assigned by management

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

Post-secondary educational degree (2 to 4-year degree from college, university, technical school, military, vocational or other advanced educational institution)

REQUIRED

Five plus years of experience in the wastewater treatment field or industrial wastewater treatment

Ability to quickly obtain State of Indiana Class D Industrial Wastewater Operator certification; either through reciprocity or testing

Experience with anaerobic and aerobic WWTP operations

Candidates are PREFERRED who offer the following:

Bachelor’s degree in biology, microbiology, Chemical or Bio-Chemical Engineering

Industrial wastewater experience strongly preferred

LANGUAGE SKILLS

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical procedures, manuals, regulations, and codes. Ability to write business reports and correspondence. Ability to communicate effectively with management, customers, employees, and external regulatory officials.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to calculate figures and amounts such as effluent quality, quantity in various forms including mg/L, lbs/day, etc.

REASONING ABILITY

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

WWTP equipment specifications and performance

Computer data entry

Understanding of permits and regulations applicable to multiple Mills in different jurisdictions

Understanding of anaerobic and aerobic wastewater treatment systems and interpretation of operational data to implement appropriate process changes

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Employees are regularly required to walk and talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Vision requirements include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, hot and cold temperatures, moving mechanical parts, and fumes or airborne particles. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

title: Crypto Options Trader
description:
You will contribute to a trading book by generating revenue and managing risk. You will build volatility models, maintain volatility surfaces, monitor Greek exposures, and execute market-making strategies. You will backtest and deploy options strategies, analyze P&L performance, and work with control functions on governance.

Responsibilities

  • Contribute to a trading book, generate revenue, and manage risk
  • Implement volatility models and maintain real-time volatility surfaces for crypto assets
  • Act as a principal market maker for crypto assets
  • Monitor Delta, Gamma, Vega, Theta, and Rho exposures
  • Develop and refine systematic strategies for short-term mispricing and market making
  • Partner with developers to backtest, prototype, and deploy options strategies
  • Develop options products for distribution
  • Perform P&L and Greek-exposure analysis to optimize trading models
  • Work with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Finance on governance and controls

Requirements

  • Have 3+ years of hands-on experience in options trading and algorithmic market making
  • Use Python
  • Understand FX, equity, and crypto market mechanics

title: Senior Cloud Architect, RAAS | Automation Services
description:
Work with a Top 20 CPA and advisory firm that Accounts for Anything. Aprio has 40 U.S. office locations, as well as international office locations and more than 3,200 team members that speak 60+ languages across the globe. By bringing together proven expertise, deep understanding, and strategic foresight for fast-growing industries, Aprio ensures clients are prepared for wherever life or business may take them. Discover a top-rated culture, vast growth opportunities and your next big career move with Aprio.

Job Sumamry

Aprio is seeking a Senior Cloud Architect to join its Risk Advisory & Assurance | Automation Services practice and help organizations design, modernize, and protect cloud environments while navigating complex cybersecurity, regulatory, and operational requirements. In this role, you will lead cloud architecture engagements from discovery through delivery, translating business, security, and compliance requirements into resilient, scalable, and supportable solutions across Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. You will serve as the senior technical authority for clients navigating cloud adoption, modernization, Zero Trust, governance, and regulated-environment initiatives while helping delivery teams apply repeatable architecture and engineering practices.
This position supports U.S. government and defense-related clients; certain engagements require personnel who are eligible to obtain a U.S. security clearance or who meet client-defined access requirements for controlled environment

What You'll Gain / Impact:

  • Opportunity to serve as the senior technical authority on high-complexity cloud transformation and cybersecurity engagements.
  • Exposure to a broad range of client environments, including U.S. government, defense, and regulated industries.
  • Ability to shape cloud strategy, architecture standards, and security practices that drive lasting organizational change.
  • Hands-on experience architecting multi-cloud solutions across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud in real-world, high-stakes environments.
  • Platform to lead, mentor, and develop architects and engineers within a growing, purpose-driven consulting practice.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead client engagements from discovery through delivery, serving as the senior technical consultant and architecture authority.
  • Facilitate executive briefings, workshops, and architecture sessions that translate business objectives, risk tolerance, and compliance obligations into actionable cloud strategies.
  • Develop current-state and target-state architectures covering applications, infrastructure, identity, networking, security, data protection, observability, resilience, and operations.
  • Design secure landing zones and cloud foundations using governance guardrails, account/subscription structures, policy enforcement, centralized logging, network segmentation, and identity-first access controls.
  • Architect hybrid and multi-cloud solutions across Microsoft Azure, AWS, and/or Google Cloud, selecting services and patterns appropriate to client requirements and risk.
  • Embed cybersecurity into architecture decisions using Zero Trust, least privilege, privileged access management, threat modeling, secure configuration, vulnerability management, encryption, and secrets management.
  • Align solutions to compliance frameworks including CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP, and other client-specific regulatory or contractual requirements.
  • Design for regulated workloads including controlled data boundaries, audit evidence, logging, data residency, secure administration, and separation of duties.
  • Provide architecture oversight during implementation, reviewing detailed designs, infrastructure-as-code, configurations, security controls, and technical deliverables for quality and conformance.
  • Partner with cybersecurity, compliance, engineering, and operations teams to resolve design tradeoffs and ensure solutions are operable, measurable, and audit-ready.
  • Evaluate and rationalize cloud services balancing security, compliance, performance, availability, cost, supportability, and time to value.
  • Develop roadmaps and migration strategies for application modernization, data migration, identity transformation, and cloud security uplift.
  • Create client-ready architecture artifacts including diagrams, decision records, control mappings, implementation plans, risk registers, and executive recommendations.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of architects and engineers while contributing to technical reviews, estimation, solution quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Support pre-sales and solution development by shaping scopes, assumptions, level-of-effort estimates, and technical approaches for complex opportunities.

Candidate Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, cybersecurity, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of progressive technology experience in architecture, engineering, cybersecurity, cloud transformation, or related consulting responsibilities.
  • 7+ years of client-facing consulting or architecture experience leading complex technical discussions and delivering tailored solutions for mid-market or enterprise organizations.
  • 5+ years of hands-on cloud architecture experience designing and implementing production solutions in Azure, AWS, and/or Google Cloud.
  • Demonstrated cybersecurity and compliance experience integrating technical controls and regulatory requirements into cloud architectures and implementation roadmaps.
  • Strong architecture communication skills with the ability to explain risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations to executives, security leaders, auditors, engineers, and business stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of architecture and security methods such as well-architected frameworks, threat modeling, shared responsibility, Zero Trust, defense-in-depth, and secure-by-design principles.
  • Ability to lead through ambiguity, manage competing requirements, drive decisions, and maintain delivery momentum across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Experience producing high-quality technical documentation including reference architectures, diagrams, standards, decision records, and implementation guidance.

Technical Depth:

Deep expertise in at least three of the following areas, with working knowledge of the others:
  • Cloud architecture: Azure, AWS, and/or Google Cloud; landing zones; hybrid connectivity; resiliency; disaster recovery; and cloud operating models.
  • Identity and access: Entra ID and cloud-native IAM; federation; Conditional Access; privileged access; just-in-time administration; workload identities; and secrets management.
  • Cloud security operations: Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Sentinel, Defender for Cloud, and/or comparable AWS or Google Cloud security services; SIEM/SOAR; detection engineering; and threat hunting.
  • Data protection: encryption, key management, data classification, DLP, Microsoft Purview or comparable services, retention, and secure data lifecycle controls.
  • Network security: segmentation, private connectivity, firewalls, secure remote administration, egress control, DNS security, web application protection, and Zero Trust network access.
  • DevSecOps and automation: infrastructure-as-code, policy-as-code, CI/CD security, configuration management, PowerShell, Python, KQL, APIs, and automated compliance validation.
  • Governance and compliance: cloud control frameworks, continuous monitoring, evidence generation, risk management, policy development, and remediation planning.

Certifications:

At least one of the following active certifications is required or must be obtained within 90 days of hire:
  • Cybersecurity and architecture: CISSP, CCSP, or SABSA certification.
  • Microsoft: AZ-305, AZ-500, or SC-100.
  • AWS: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional or AWS Certified Security – Specialty.
  • Google Cloud: Professional Cloud Architect or Professional Cloud Security Engineer.
Additional cloud, security, networking, DevOps, or compliance certifications are preferred. Active certifications are required for consideration.

Preferred Experience:

  • Architecture for U.S. Government or defense-related environments including Azure Government, Microsoft 365 GCC High, AWS GovCloud (US), or comparable regulated cloud platforms.
  • Implementing or assessing controls for CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP, DoD impact levels, or similar frameworks.
  • Application and platform modernization including containers, Kubernetes, serverless architectures, APIs, data platforms, and cloud-native integration patterns.
  • Cloud financial governance including cost allocation, optimization, forecasting, and architecture decisions informed by FinOps practices.
  • Technical leadership in consulting delivery including mentoring, quality assurance, reusable intellectual property, and support for proposals or statements of work.

title: Electrical and Instrumentation Technician
description:
Electrical and Instrumentation Technician installs, services, troubleshoots, and performs preventive and predictive maintenance functions on plant equipment. This equipment includes but is not limited to; plant lighting equipment, electrical circuits, motors, starters, motor control centers, programmable controllers, control panels, transformers, switches, transmitters, automatic valves, regulators, guide systems, distributed control systems, PLC's, overhead cranes, etc. May perform additional duties as assigned. The Electrical and Instrumentation Technician must be able to read orders, possess basic to intermediate math skills, read and understand technical manuals and literature and be able to operate motorized equipment such as forklifts, scissor lifts, Genie lifts, hoists and cranes.

  1. Able to troubleshoot, repair, and wire 120 volt and (3) phase 460 volt AC circuits and electrical equipment.
  2. Able to troubleshoot, repair, and wire 24 volt DC control circuits.
  3. Basic understanding of Electricity and Instrumentation.
  4. Able to troubleshoot, repair, and install distribution systems up to 460 volts.
  5. Able to troubleshoot, repair, and install controls: coils contactors, relays, brakes etc.
  6. Able to install transformers up to 460 volts.
  7. Able to safely rack in and rack out 460 volt, 4160 volt, and 12.47 kV breakers.
  8. Able to interpret PID, hydraulic, pneumatic and wiring drawings / diagrams.
  9. Able to wire motors single phase, 3 phase 460 volt and 3 phase 4160 volt as per NEC / OSHA codes and Pratt standard operating procedures.
  10. Able to use and interpret a Megohm meter.
  11. Able to use and interpret a multimeter; volts, amps and ohms
  12. Able to troubleshoot and install switches; proximity, speed, limit, pressure etc.
  13. Basic understanding and repair of guiding systems.
  14. Able to run and bend conduit and pull wire.
  15. Able to troubleshoot control valves and transmitters.
  16. General knowledge of electrical and pneumatic systems in mill.
  17. Understanding of pneumatic controls including controllers, actuators, positioners, and valves.
  18. Demonstrate knowledge of where to find equipment I/O for various processes.

Education and/or Experience:

Post-secondary educational degree (2 to 4 year degree from college, university, technical-school, military, vocational or other advanced educational institution) is required.

Essential Job Functions:

  1. Mental Ability - Must be able to read orders & prepare reports legibly and properly. Must be able to communicate orally with all personnel in the plant. Must be able to operate a calculator for basic mathematical computations. Basic typing skills are essential because shift logs, reports, and emails must be composed.
  1. Physical Ability- The Electrical and Instrumentation Technician must be able to work with hand and power tools and requires manual dexterity with both hands. Must be able climb in and out of motorized equipment and be able to operate two foot pedals as well as operate both hands/arms for driving and lift controls. Must have excellent depth perception to maneuver motorized equipment around crowded areas with co-workers nearby. Manual lifting of items is frequent. Must be able to move, position, and climb ladders in a safe manner.
  1. Safety - It is plant policy to work in a safe manner. All Electrical and Instrumentation Technicians must ensure guards are in place, follow plant & safety rules, policies, and procedures. Must secure all open electrical panels and insure that all abandoned wiring is disconnected from all power sources. Must follow the posted PPE requirements for arc-flash protection. PPE must be worn per posted plant regulations when work on energized circuits is required. Eye protection must be worn when cutting, drilling or other machining operations are performed. Hearing protection must be worn at all times. Must follow lockout/ tag out procedures and assist with lockout/tag out for maintenance and operations tasks. Knowledge of pneumatic and hydraulic circuits is necessary to help insure safe lockout/tag outs. Must be able to lift items up to 50 lbs. in a safe manner and determine when help is needed to lift heavier items. Attendance to all Safety Meetings is mandatory.

Physical Description:

Work can be physically and mentally demanding at times. Electrical and Instrumentation Technicians must be able to physically change valves, transmitters, and small motors as needed. Must be able to observe immediate and overall areas for electrical hazards and take appropriate action. Simple rigging skills are required. Sweeping and mopping MCC and other work areas and emptying garbage cans is required. Cleaning up leaks and spills is required as needed.

Additional Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Requirements:

  • Wear all required Personal Protective Equipment (glasses, ear plugs, shoes, gloves, etc…)
  • Drug testing/Screening, Background Checks, Physical exam, and Reference Checks
  • Demonstrates a proven record of learning aptitude
  • Participate in ongoing educational certificate training program provided
  • Housekeeping, including washing up, sweeping, and shoveling debris.
  • Working knowledge of equipment design for process troubleshooting.
  • Perform other tasks as required by Mill Management.

Salary Compensation

Electrical & Instrumentation Technicians will be Salaried Non-Exempt (qualify for overtime above 40 hrs./week)

There is built-in overtime with the (4) four shift rotating schedule

Mill Incentive Program: Monthly maximum of 33.3% of Base Salary (Paid Quarterly)

Total Compensation: Ability to earn $100,000.00+ per year with base salary, overtime, and incentive plan

Additional Opportunities for Salary Increases:

title: Network and Cloud Administrator
description:
Position Announcement: Network and Cloud Administrator

Northeastern Junior College is seeking an enthusiastic and self-motivated individual to serve as the Network and Cloud Administrator. Responsibilities include hardware and software support to students, faculty, and staff. This position is accountable for the installation, configuration, management, research, and evaluation of all LAN/WAN/WLAN hardware/software (routers, switches, access points). This position maintains the campus-wide Cisco Meraki and Splash Access dashboards, is the Cloud product lead administrator (Entra ID, Exchange Admin, Intune, Cisco Control Hub), endpoint security and telephony administrator. Other responsibilities include recording technology inventory regarding infrastructure and telephone support for general hardware and software issues. This position is responsible for server administration duties pertaining to Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM), DNS, DHCP, and print servers.

Questions regarding the position may be directed to Kade Roelle, NJC Information Technology Director at 970-521-6787 or e-mail to: kade.roelle@njc.edu. For more information about NJC, see the college website at .

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be:

General IT Support

  • Provide day-to-day technical support as part of the IT Help Desk.
  • Assist faculty, staff, and students with technology troubleshooting.
  • Install, update, customize, and maintain hardware and software, for desktop computers, notebook computers, including all peripherals, accessories, and printing devices.

Network Administration

  • Physically lays out and maintains a LAN/WAN/WLAN by configuring and installing hardware, checks connections and removes or replaces components in servers, access points, switches, and routers within the network.
  • Manages and configures NJC's Cisco Meraki and Splash Access Dashboards.
  • Manage NJC's student residence hall network infrastructure including Meraki and Cisco Systems.
  • Research and evaluate network equipment to develop life cycle plans.
  • Manages campus DHCP and DNS.
  • Lead contact for Firewall provisioning working alongside the Colorado Community College System.
  • Configure and troubleshoot VoIP telephones.

Cloud Administration

  • Provide administration of Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange Admin, Intune, and Cisco Control Hub.
  • Support hybrid identity infrastructure including Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, and modern authentication standards.
  • Maintain expertise in Microsoft cloud platforms and ensure proper system configuration and access controls.
  • Configure and troubleshoot Cloud Telephony.

Server Administration

  • Administer Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM), DHCP, DNS, and print servers.
  • Configure the applications running on the servers and apply updates to the systems.
  • Troubleshoot SCCM, DHCP, DNS, and print services.

Endpoint Security

  • Manage NJC's endpoint security platform (Windows Defender).
  • Serve as NJC's lead representative on the statewide Cybersecurity team at the system level.
  • Stay knowledgeable about policies, laws, and issues affecting endpoint security.

Other Duties

  • Perform additional duties as assigned by the supervisor, including participation in committees and special projects.
  • Support both short-term and long-term institutional initiatives as needed.

What You Will Need:

  • Demonstrated experience with network and IT organization and documentation.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate with diverse groups including faculty, administrators, technical teams, and external agencies.
  • Network equipment life cycle planning skills and cost analysis.
  • Proven problem solving, troubleshooting, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex systems simultaneously.
  • Must have a high level of positive energy, be a self-starter, and a team player with excellent motivation skills and the desire to excel and promote Northeastern Junior College.

What We Require:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology or a closely related field from an accredited college or university.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in:
    • Enterprise networks (LAN/WAN, Wi Fi 6E/7, Cisco Catalyst, Cisco Meraki, Splash Access).
    • Structured cabling standards (CAT6A/CAT7, Fiber-Optic)
    • DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP and other Protocols
    • Cloud platform and infrastructure management (Entra ID, Exchange Admin, Intune, Autopilot, Cisco Control Hub).
    • Server management and configuration (Windows Server 2025)
    • Endpoint security (Microsoft Defender)
    • Help desk and IT service management (ITIL practices preferred)

What We Can Offer:

This is a full-time professional appointment. Annual salary is $62,000-$70,000, depending on qualifications and experience. Competitive fringe benefit package available which includes medical, dental, life, PERA Retirement Plan, 11 paid holidays, and several optional benefits. Position begins as soon as a qualified candidate is identified.

title: Senior Engineer, Reliability (R6440)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

We are seeking a Senior Reliability Engineer to lead reliability engineering activities for the development, integration, testing, and operation of aircraft systems. This position will work across engineering disciplines to establish reliability requirements, manage system reliability budgets, perform reliability analyses, and identify design improvements that increase aircraft availability and mission success.

The successful candidate will have direct experience working on aircraft or other complex aerospace systems and be proficient with industry-standard reliability tools and methods. This engineer will serve as the primary reliability point of contact for assigned programs and communicate reliability performance, risks, and improvement plans to engineering leadership and customers.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and maintain aircraft-level reliability requirements, objectives, and program reliability plans.
  • Establish, allocate, and manage reliability budgets across systems, subsystems, and line-replaceable units.
  • Track predicted reliability against program targets and identify components or subsystems driving reliability risk.
  • Perform reliability predictions using component failure-rate data, operating environments, and mission profiles.
  • Conduct Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), and Reliability Block Diagram (RBD) analysis.
  • Support aircraft system safety assessments by providing failure rates, failure modes, and reliability data.
  • Develop and maintain Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF), Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF), mission reliability, availability, and related reliability metrics.
  • Perform reliability allocation, trade studies, sensitivity analyses, and design assessments.
  • Lead or support Failure Reporting, Analysis, and Corrective Action System (FRACAS) activities.
  • Analyze ground-test, flight-test, supplier, maintenance, and field-performance data to identify reliability trends.
  • Apply Weibull analysis and other statistical methods to evaluate failure behavior and predict component life.
  • Work with design teams to eliminate single-point failures, reduce high-risk failure modes, and improve fault tolerance.
  • Review supplier reliability analyses, test results, and supporting technical data.
  • Define reliability demonstration and growth-test requirements, success criteria, and data-collection needs.
  • Support technical reviews, including SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, and reliability review boards.
  • Communicate reliability performance, budget status, assumptions, risks, and recommended corrective actions to customers and program leadership.
  • Mentor junior engineers and improve organizational reliability processes, tools, and standards.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in reliability engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related technical field
  • 5+ years of related experience in reliability engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related technical field
  • Direct experience supporting aircraft development, integration, testing, sustainment, or operations.
  • Experience developing and managing reliability budgets at the system, subsystem, or equipment level.
  • Proficiency with reliability methods such as FMEA/FMECA, FTA, RBD, Weibull analysis, reliability predictions, and FRACAS.
  • Familiarity with reliability metrics such as MTBF, MTBCF, failure rate, mission reliability, operational availability, and inherent availability.
  • Experience using reliability analysis tools such as ReliaSoft, Windchill Quality Solutions, Isograph, RAM Commander, or equivalent.
  • Ability to interpret aircraft mission profiles, operating environments, duty cycles, and test data.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary engineering teams and suppliers.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, presentation, and customer communication skills.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any security clearance required for the program.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working on military aircraft, unmanned aircraft, or other defense aerospace platforms.
  • Experience managing aircraft-level reliability allocations and flowing requirements down to suppliers.
  • Familiarity with MIL-HDBK-217, NPRD, EPRD, RIAC 217Plus, or equivalent reliability prediction methods and databases.
  • Experience integrating reliability engineering with system safety, maintainability, logistics, and availability analyses.
  • Knowledge of Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) and condition-based maintenance approaches.
  • Experience supporting environmental qualification, ground testing, flight testing, or reliability growth testing.
  • Familiarity with Model-Based Systems Engineering and requirements management tools.
  • Certified Reliability Engineer credentials or equivalent professional certification.
  • Active U.S. security clearance.

title: UX Designer (Remote)
description:
RainFocus, one of the most innovative software companies, is in search of an exceptional UX Designer.
About RainFocus
RainFocus cares about its employees, customers, and the world in which we live. Our rapidly growing team serves Fortune 500 companies like Adobe, Cisco, IBM, Oracle, VMware, and others to prepare and execute in-person, virtual, and hybrid events, across the world. Those events are delivered through our industry-disrupting software platform, with groundbreaking business intelligence, to elevate the attendee experience, streamline event operations, and accelerate marketing results. We are well-funded, growing fast, and building a company that is changing the market — it will be challenging, fun and exciting.
About the Role
You’ll play an important part in the entire product development process, from brainstorming to launch. You’ll be part of a UX team where each designer is responsible for different areas of our product and integrated into individual scrum teams. They work closely with the Product Manager and Developers to create elegant solutions to problems our customers are facing. The product team also includes front-end developers who share our passion to deliver a great user experience throughout our platform.

What You'll Do:

  • Shape ideas into testable bets

  • Partner with stakeholders and executives to capture strategic ideas and turn them into clear hypotheses

  • Define the problem, the target customer, the business case, and the evidence that would change our minds

  • Push back constructively when an idea lacks a clear problem or buyer

Lead discovery research

  • Plan and run high-volume discovery with customers and prospects, including interviews, workshops, concept tests, and usability sessions

  • Work with Stakeholders, Sales, and Customer Success to find the right participants quickly

  • Synthesize findings into short, decision-ready insights

Build proof-of-concept prototypes

  • Create interactive prototypes, from clickable concepts to functional PoCs, using AI-assisted tools

  • Apply sound UX judgment to flows, information architecture, and interaction design

  • Work with your developer counterpart to draw a clear line between prototype-grade and production-ready, and hand off cleanly

  • Use PoCs to confirm understanding, not to deliver solutions

Validate against the market

  • Test willingness to adopt and pay, not just whether people like the idea

  • Define success signals before each validation cycle and track them

  • Present recommendations to leadership with the evidence behind them

Protect the integrity of the process

  • Frame every prototype clearly as exploratory so customers never hear a commitment

  • Work with Sales and Legal on NDAs, disclosure, and expectation-setting

  • Keep Sales informed of what you're learning and what is, and isn't, safe to say to customers

Lead the pod

  • Set priorities, rhythm, and working agreements for a small cross-functional team

  • Share frequent, brief readouts instead of big-bang reviews

  • Build reusable templates, scripts, and prototype patterns that make each cycle faster

What this role does NOT do

  • Build or customize solutions for a specific customer

  • Help customers integrate, configure, or implement our software

  • Make roadmap or delivery commitments based purely on a PoC

  • Ship production code (engineering reviews and rebuilds PoCs before anything goes to market)

What Success Looks Like:

Success is measured by the quality of the decision, not by whether an idea moves forward. A well-evidenced "stop" is a win.

  • Ideas reach a go/no-go decision in weeks, not quarters

  • Ideas the business funds are backed by clear problem definitions, working prototypes, and customer proof

  • Leadership and Sales trust the evidence and understand why ideas advanced or stopped

  • Fewer fully built features fail to find demand

What You Bring:

Core skills

  • Strong business thinking: markets, buyers, pricing, and ROI, not just usability

  • Demonstrated rapid prototyping ability, including fluency with AI-assisted building tools

  • Hands-on discovery research experience and comfort talking directly with customers and prospects, including senior stakeholders

  • UX and product design fundamentals, with a portfolio or examples of shipped work

  • Product management experience or equivalent: scoping, prioritization, and stakeholder management

Also valuable

  • B2B SaaS experience, especially enterprise software

  • Comfort working in or alongside a live codebase

  • Experience leading small teams without formal authority

  • The confidence to tell senior leaders "the evidence doesn't support this"

How this role is different

  • From a traditional PM: less roadmap ownership, more hypothesis testing, and you build the artifacts yourself

  • From a UX Designer: you own the business case and market validation, not just the experience

Location
This remote role can be located anywhere in the United States of America.
Why work at RainFocus?
At RainFocus we delight millions of attendees at large-scale events by delivering better insights, experiences, and marketing. We were able to pivot our product and services offering in 2020 to continue growing and serving new clients and events.
As a member of the RainFocus team, you will have the opportunity to experience first-hand the impact of our platform at events around the world. Additionally, RainFocus offers competitive salaries, competitive benefits, 401k, generous PTO, and countless other team building activities.
What are you waiting for? Apply today! We need more talented, hard-working, fun-loving team members just like yourself!

title: Senior Data Engineer (AV) Hybrid - Full Time - Technology United Arab Emirates
description:
Senior Data Engineer (AV)

Department: Geo Cluster

Employment Type: Full Time

Description

About the role
We are preparing the data foundation for our autonomous-driving work, and we are hiring the engineer who will start it. Today we collect street-level imagery and GPS tracks from vehicle cameras, including our own camera units with NVIDIA edge devices on board, and use them to update maps. Next comes a dedicated survey vehicle with a full sensor set: multi-camera, IMU, LiDAR. You will start with the imagery and map data pipelines we run today, and as the sensor platform arrives, you will build the pipelines that turn its data into training datasets for autonomous-driving models.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build the pipelines that move multi-sensor data (multi-camera video, IMU, LiDAR, GPS) from vehicles into cloud storage, synchronize and geo-reference the streams
  • Own the storage layout and lifecycle for sensor data: partitioning, hot and archival tiers, cost control as volume grows
  • Build validation and monitoring on the ingest path: incomplete uploads, missing or unsynchronized streams, vehicles that stopped producing usable data
  • Prepare training datasets for autonomous-driving models: select data by location, route, and conditions, version datasets, and deliver them in the formats ML teams need
  • Until then: take over and develop the current imagery and GPS-track pipelines from vehicle cameras, and contribute to geodata pipelines (ingestion from company data, OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps and vendors, conflation, validation, publication)
  • Work with company data in BigQuery and keep spatial queries fast on large PostGIS and GeoParquet tables

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

  • 4+ years in data engineering
  • Experience with multi-sensor data from vehicles or robots: cameras, IMU or LiDAR, and keeping the streams in sync
  • Experience preparing training datasets for computer vision or autonomous-driving models.
  • Large volumes of binary or media data in object storage (S3 or GCS); distributed processing (Spark or equivalent)
  • Hands-on experience with spatial data: PostGIS, GeoPandas/Shapely, coordinate reference systems, GPS tracks
  • Strong Python and SQL; AWS or GCP, Docker, Kubernetes

Nice to have

  • Sensor data formats such as ROS2 bag, MCAP or point clouds
  • Parquet, Delta or Iceberg; Databricks
  • Argo Workflows or Airflow
  • OpenStreetMap and Overture Map
  • QGIS
  • BigQuery

Why join us

  • Help us challenge injustice by creating fair choices for millions of people across 47 countries.
  • Develop your professional skills with access to mentoring, career consulting, and learning programs
  • Collaborate with teams around the world and gain international experience through our Global Talent Exchange Program
  • Engage in company-wide challenges, awards, sports activities, employee-led social impact and volunteering projects
  • Work alongside people who take initiative, speak openly, and challenge themselves to grow

title: Fleet Technicians
description:
Fleet Technicians All Levels

Fleet Maintenance Career Opportunities

Pay

$18.39–$45.04 per hour starting rates, based on classification

Location

Tampa, Florida

Employment

Based on available vacancy

Closing date

Open continuously

Requisition

Evergreen candidate pool

Area of interest

Maintenance

Keep Our Community Moving

Hillsborough Transit Authority (HART) is accepting applications on an ongoing basis for Fleet Technician opportunities at multiple skill and certification levels. From technicians developing their mechanical expertise to experienced ASE-certified professionals, our team helps keep fleet vehicles safe, reliable and ready to serve the community.

This evergreen requisition builds a candidate pool for current and future vacancies. Openings at every classification may not be available at all times. Qualified applicants may be contacted as opportunities become available. Applying does not guarantee an interview or employment.

Candidates will be considered for classifications that match their documented education, experience and certifications. The specific classification, duties and applicable contractual pay will be confirmed during the selection and offer process.

Why Choose HART

  • Put your technical skills to work supporting dependable public transportation.
  • Contribute to a team that values quality workmanship, safety and vehicle reliability.
  • Explore opportunities across technician classifications, with starting pay established by the applicable union contract.

What You Will Do

  • Perform preventive maintenance, inspections and routine servicing of fleet vehicles and equipment.
  • Diagnose mechanical problems and perform repairs appropriate to your classification, training and qualifications.
  • Inspect vehicles, systems and components for wear, damage, defects and potential safety concerns.
  • Maintain accurate work orders, maintenance records, inspection reports and related documentation.
  • Use tools, diagnostic equipment and shop equipment safely and effectively.
  • Maintain a clean, organized work area and follow maintenance procedures, safety requirements and departmental policies.
  • Collaborate with Fleet Maintenance team members to support vehicle availability, reliability and timely repairs. Perform other related duties as assigned.

What Success Looks Like

  • Reliable service. Preventive maintenance and timely repairs help keep fleet vehicles available for service.
  • Quality workmanship. Inspections and repairs meet established maintenance procedures and the requirements of the technician’s classification.
  • Safe operations. Tools, equipment and work areas are maintained and used safely.
  • Accurate documentation. Work orders, inspection reports and maintenance records are complete and clear.

What You Bring

Required for All Levels

  • High school diploma or General Educational Development (GED) certificate.
  • Ability to understand and follow written and verbal instructions and established safety procedures.
  • Ability to collaborate with team members and maintain a professional, safety-focused work environment.
  • Willingness to learn, maintain technical proficiency and develop fleet maintenance and repair skills.

Preferred

  • Previous experience in a public transit maintenance environment.

Classification Requirements and Starting Pay

Starting hourly rates are established by the applicable union contract. Applicants must meet the requirements of the classification for which they are considered.

Technician Apprentice

Starting pay: $18.39 per hour

  • Graduation from or current attendance at a diesel or mechanical technical school is preferred.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and at least one (1) year of experience in automotive or diesel repair, servicing and maintenance.
  • Successful completion of the training and testing requirements of the registered apprenticeship program within six (6) months of hire.

Fleet Technician B

Starting pay: $24.34 per hour

  • Graduation from a diesel or mechanical technical school is preferred.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and at least one (1) year of experience in automotive or diesel repair, servicing and maintenance.

Fleet Technician A

Starting pay: $29.07 per hour

  • At least two (2) years of experience in automotive servicing and maintenance.
  • At least four (4) ASE certifications: H-series or T-series for Bus Technicians; A-series for Paratransit Technicians.
  • Must successfully obtain Universal EPA Section 608 and Section 609 air-conditioning certifications.

Senior Fleet Technician

Starting pay: $33.76 per hour

  • At least two (2) years of experience in automotive servicing and maintenance.
  • A certificate and six (6) months of vocational training. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.
  • At least seven (7) ASE certifications: H-series or T-series for Bus Technicians; A-series for Paratransit Technicians.
  • Current Universal EPA Section 608 and Section 609 air-conditioning certifications.

ASE Certified Fleet Technician

Starting pay: $45.04 per hour

  • At least four (4) years of experience in automotive servicing and maintenance.
  • A certificate and six (6) months of vocational training. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.
  • At least seven (7) ASE certifications: H-series or T-series for Bus Technicians; A-series for Paratransit Technicians.
  • ASE Master Technician certification: H-series or T-series Master certification for Bus Technicians; A-series Master certification for Paratransit Technicians.
  • Current Universal EPA Section 608 and Section 609 air-conditioning certifications.

Work Environment and Physical Demands

Fleet Technicians work in maintenance shops, garages and potentially outdoor environments, with exposure to vehicles, tools, machinery, lubricants and other materials associated with vehicle maintenance and repair. The work requires the ability to perform the physical tasks of the applicable classification, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Safety and Security Responsibilities

Follow established maintenance procedures, safety requirements and departmental policies. Use tools, diagnostic equipment and shop equipment safely, maintain an organized work area, and identify and report potential safety concerns.

Apply to Join HART

Apply through HART Employment and identify the technician classification or classifications that match your qualifications. Include your relevant maintenance experience, technical education and current certifications. Applications will be reviewed as current and future staffing needs arise.

View full job descriptions and apply at https://www.gohart.org/Pages/about-hart-employment.aspx

Equal Employment Opportunity and Accommodations

HART is an equal opportunity employer committed to a workplace free from unlawful discrimination. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, experience, skills and organizational needs in accordance with applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available during the application and interview process.

This requisition describes the general nature and level of work and is not an exhaustive list of duties, qualifications or working conditions. Employees may perform other related duties as assigned.

  • Experience reliably handling thousands of concurrent connections
  • Non-trivial systems programming projects, major inference-engine open-source contributions, or deep-dive technical write-ups

  • PhD in CS, Physics, or Math, or equivalent practical experience building backend or ML systems
  • Professional fluency in written and spoken English

title: Risk and Compliance Specialist
description:
BIS Safety Software is a SaaS company on a mission to change how organizations manage safety, learning, and compliance. Our clients trust us with their people's training records and personal information, and we take that trust seriously. We are looking for a Risk and Compliance Specialist to own our compliance program day to day: the audits, the controls behind them, and the risk calls that keep us on side all year.

About the Role:

This is a role for someone who already knows compliance and is ready to own it, not just support it. Audit season matters, but the real work happens in the months between. You’ll keep our program sharp so the audit itself is the easy part.

You’ll also be the go-to voice on risk, data, and privacy across the company. One day that’s a tricky client request, the next it’s a vendor decision or a security question that needs an answer by end of day. You’ll help shape how BIS handles trust, and every team here will feel your work.

This is an in-person role based out of our Sherwood Park, Alberta office.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

  • Help lead our SOC 2 audit and PCI DSS attestation, scoping the work, assigning action items across departments, following up on deadlines, and collecting the evidence that gets us through cleanly
  • Own control documentation for each framework and work with every team to confirm their controls are current and holding up
  • Lead and contribute to risk assessments across the business, documenting risks, recommending mitigation, and following through until each one is resolved or escalated
  • Review in-scope vendors that handle personal information, financial data, or client data
  • Manage the Risk and Compliance and Privacy inboxes, answering client tickets on privacy, data, and personal information with clear, accurate guidance
  • Keep our privacy policy, terms and conditions, and subprocessor list current, and flag when changes in law or the industry mean something needs a second look
  • Complete the privacy, data security, and data retention sections of RFPs and security questionnaires
  • Partner with IT and Technology on risk, offering practical solutions, separating true must-haves from best-practice suggestions, and teaching along the way
  • Coordinate quick cross-team reviews when an urgent issue or emerging risk lands

You might be the right fit if you:

  • Catch what's missed. Attention to detail is the single most important trait for this role, and you look past the original ask to see the whole picture
  • Have kept a SOC 2 program running, not just sat in on the audit, and can walk through what good pre-audit prep looks like
  • Juggle many large projects at once with an audit lens: dozens of action items, several departments, and different deadlines, all tracked and closed out on time
  • Speak up. You're comfortable raising considerations when it matters, and you know how to make your case
  • Ask the right questions first. You figure out what's actually needed, and how much it matters to the client, before committing hours to it
  • Shift gears when something urgent lands without losing track of everything else
  • Adapt your approach to the situation instead of applying one way of doing compliance to every problem
  • Own the work without waiting for permission or step-by-step direction
  • Build real working relationships across teams, because this role touches almost every department here

Qualifications we are looking for:

  • 2+ years of hands-on compliance experience
  • SOC 2 experience, including maintaining ongoing control documentation and coordinating audit deliverables across departments
  • PCI DSS and/or GDPR experience
  • Strong data fluency: subprocessors, data controllers vs. processors, data governance and retention, and how information flows across systems
  • Post-secondary education in a relevant field, or equivalent experience
  • Tech-savvy and comfortable working with AI tools, as you'll be in our software every day and use AI to support compliance work
  • Experience with Microsoft 365

Bonus points if you have:

  • An IT, SaaS, or software-side compliance background, especially around data management and data controls
  • Privacy knowledge, including Canadian privacy law
  • Certifications such as CIPP/C or CIPM
  • Cybersecurity knowledge
  • Experience completing RFPs or security questionnaires

Compensation and benefits:

  • Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
  • Full medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Life insurance and disability insurance
  • Health spending account
  • Flexible working hours
  • On-the-job training and growth opportunities
  • Free on-site parking

About BIS:

BIS Safety Software has been headquartered in Sherwood Park, Alberta, since 2006. We build software that helps organizations manage safety training, learning, and compliance - and we're growing!

A few things that make us different: we don't use job titles internally - we value humility and contribution over hierarchy. We move fast, integrate new ideas quickly, and give people real ownership of their work. And through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), you have the opportunity to own a piece of the company you're helping build.

How to apply:

With your application, please include a short cover letter about a SOC 2 audit you helped coordinate: what your part was, and one thing you'd do differently next time.

Visit our Careers Page for more information. We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest. Only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Product Manager
description:

Introduction:

Carrier Enterprise, a leading national distributor of residential and light commercial HVAC products, is seeking a dynamic Product Manager for Parts & Supplies. Join a team that excels in providing top-notch HVAC/R products, parts, and supplies through licensed HVAC/R dealers and contractors.

Company Description:

Carrier Enterprise (CE) is a premier national distributor specializing in residential and light commercial Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) products, parts, and supplies. We serve licensed HVAC/R dealers and contractors, ensuring top-quality HVAC solutions across 28 states, Puerto Rico, the Caribbean, Latin America, Mexico, and Canada. With over 200+ locations, we are well-positioned to meet our customers' HVAC/R needs.

Company Website:

www.carrierenterprise.com

Job Summary:

The Product Manager will be responsible for leading critical cross functional product development of new and existing product lines while identifying, understanding, defining, and prioritizing the future of our product assortment to support our business growth plan. The position will be responsible for product assortment, marketing, programs, promotions, product pricing, vendor negotiations, product training, monitoring, tracking, and analyzing product performance, product SKU maintenance, and managing non-performing inventory for parts and supplies across product sectors.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain sales strategy with regional representatives for all wholesale product offerings for all sales channels.
  • Develop, implement, manage, and communicate all facets of new product introduction from strategy to pricing, marketing, PIM coordination, inventory planning, product roll-out and execution on all product offerings in all sales channels for Parts and Supplies.
  • Evaluate competitive product and pricing data. Communicate with factory and sales teams on advantages and disadvantages, product gaps and voice of customer.
  • Recommend sell price positioning (max and min) to maximize market share and company profit margins.
  • Partners with Regional Pricing and Demand Planning groups to create assortment, pricing, and stocking levels for the Region.
  • Conduct regular visits to regional branches to execute performance checklists, audit local product needs, and ensure alignment with HQ strategic initiatives.
  • Lead regional requirements for branch merchandising, showroom displays, and planogramming initiatives to maximize parts and supplies product awareness
  • Coordinate and manage specialized regional programs, including Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) and Factory Authorized Parts (FAP) requirements across identified sales channels
  • Identify, coordinate, and facilitate required product and technical training programs for internal regional personnel and external customers
  • Provide oversight and assist regional sell-through and disposition of all products, parts and supplies
  • Identifies and removes roadblocks and obstacles that may impair product launches, execution, and deadlines to ensure we meet strategic, sales and marketing goals.
  • Develop, implement, manage internal, external and factory marketing programs in conjunction with both Carrier Enterprise HQ and Regional Marketing Directors.
  • Drives new and existing products through the stage gate process and facilitates full product execution launch. This includes but not limited to managing model supersedes, new SKU set up and designation through all stages of stage gate.
  • Defines and drives objectives on product launches and promotions providing the Concept, Features & Benefits, Customer Segmentation and Pricing Strategy.
  • Coordinates with Carrier Corp Regional Product Specific Sales Manager activities with sales team.
  • Provide oversight on all products for CE Regional reporting on a monthly/quarterly cadence for CE leadership, Carrier Corporation, and share-holder review.
  • Conducts vendor mid-year and annual reviews on movement, marketing plans and reviews performance feedback.
  • Support sales teams in all customer channels with joint customer sales calls.
  • Provide oversight for overall regional product specific Market Funds in conjunction with the CE HQ Marketing department.
  • Manage repository of product and parts and supplies, sales, and pricing information to be accessible by all sales team channels.
  • Evaluate, understand, communicate, and manage State, Local Utility rebates impacting all products, parts and supplies segments.
  • Evaluate, understand, communicate, and manage State, Local and National mandates and changes impacting all products, parts, and supplies segments.

Required Qualifications:

  • 3 - 5+ years Product Management, Product Sales experience in a high-ranking HVAC or related Product Management position.
  • Proven track record in the HVAC industry, ideally in products, services, technology, product management or in a specialized sales capacity
  • Diverse experience in product marketing, product assortment planning, and new product introduction with the ability to leverage new product innovations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft applications and Salesforce
  • Strong analytical, technical, verbal, and written communication skills
  • Knowledge of product strategy and its relationship to the Wholesale HVAC industry
  • Highly organized with the ability to prioritize and track multiple tasks to successful completion
  • Exceptional leadership and managerial skills
  • A rich blend of analytical, creative, strategic, and tactical talent

  • Tuition Reimbursement & Professional Development

title: Lead Data Engineer - Data Migration & Lakehouse

You thrive on turning decades of legacy complexity into clean, modern data architecture. You feel at home navigating undocumented mainframes, tangled schemas, and ambiguous specs — and you know how to translate that chaos into a clear technical path forward. If you love owning complex migrations end-to-end, building trust with stakeholders through clarity and honesty, and shaping how data moves from legacy into the lakehouse era — this is for you.

Your Tasks

  • Migration Ownership: Lead large-scale migration projects from legacy systems (ranging from SQL over ERP to mainframes) into modern cloud/lakehouse targets, taking full technical responsibility.
  • Databricks Architecture: Design and implement robust pipelines using Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, and Databricks Asset Bundles for CI/CD-style deployment.
  • Data Modeling & Reconciliation: Own data modeling, schema mapping, and reconciliation across heterogeneous systems, resolving structural mismatches independently.
  • Discovery & Assessment Leadership: Reviewing source documentation, interviewing SMEs, producing gap analyses, and translating ambiguous or outdated specs into concrete technical requirements.
  • Data Quality & Validation: Establish data quality frameworks and automated validation as team standards.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Proactively surface risks — documentation gaps, structural mismatches — clearly and early to non-technical stakeholders, representing SQUER with confidence.

Your Qualifications

  • Must-Haves
    • Migration Track Record: 5+ years in data engineering, with several large-scale legacy-to-cloud/lakehouse migrations led independently.
    • Databricks Depth: Hands-on mastery of the Databricks ecosystem — Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, and Asset Bundles for CI/CD-style deployment.
    • Data Modeling & Reconciliation: Strong command of data modeling and schema mapping across heterogeneous systems, from mainframes to legacy ERPs.
    • Discovery Experience: Experience in discovery/assessment phases end-to-end — interviewing SMEs, identifying gaps between legacy systems and target architecture, turning ambiguity into concrete requirements.
    • Data Quality Rigor: Practical experience with data quality frameworks and automated validation (e.g., Great Expectations, dbt tests, custom reconciliation tooling).
    • Communication & Risk Ownership: Ability to break down complex topics and surface risks early and clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
    • AI-Assisted Workflows: Comfort using AI/LLM-assisted tooling in a data pipeline context.
  • Nice-to-Haves
    • Experience with legacy system archaeology (undocumented COBOL/mainframe systems, EDI, proprietary ERPs)
    • Exposure to agentic AI
    • Metadata management or data catalog tooling beyond Unity Catalog
    • Experience building or evaluating LLM-based mapping/matching tools (schema matching, entity resolution)
Why You'll Love Working at SQUER:
  • Ownership & Responsibility: at SQUER, we believe in empowering our team. In our flat hierarchies, your ideas and actions matter more than titles. Take the reins, make an impact and grow with us.
  • Learn & Grow: Tap into a € 5.000 annual training budget to sharpen your skills and take advantage of our in-house Leadership Academy. Join and be part of our active tech community through meetups, hackathons and training sessions. Get up to 40h/year additional time off for your personal education.
  • Exciting Challenges & Real Impact: Dive into diverse projects where your work truly makes a difference – for our clients and for SQUER.
  • Flexibility for Performance: Benefit from hybrid work options, flexible hours, workations within the EU, and additional vacation days – giving you the freedom to perform at your best.
  • Tailored Tools for Success: Choose your preferred hardware configuration and leverage our suite of AI tools and licenses (Anthropic, OpenAI, and more) to suit your working style.
  • We Value You: Beyond perks and benefits, we offer a competitive annual salary to recognize your exceptional contributions.
  • Be Part of a Thriving Team Culture: At SQUER, collaboration and connection are at the heart of what we do. Through open communication, shared successes, and meaningful team events – including our annual SQUER offsite – we cultivate a culture where everyone feels valued and inspired to grow together.
  • A Perks-Packed Workplace: Work in a central office with a spacious terrace and BBQ, enjoy free lunch in the office, MyClubs sports membership, and either a free “Wiener Linien” ticket or a partial contribution to the “Klimaticket”. Plus, benefit from free massages, referral bonuses, Corporate Benefits, and JobRad. Annual employee presents and a monthly team breakfast add extra value to your work experience.
