description:
Work with a Top 20 CPA and advisory firm that Accounts for Anything. Aprio has 40 U.S. office locations, as well as international office locations and more than 3,200 team members that speak 60+ languages across the globe. By bringing together proven expertise, deep understanding, and strategic foresight for fast-growing industries, Aprio ensures clients are prepared for wherever life or business may take them. Discover a top-rated culture, vast growth opportunities and your next big career move with Aprio.

Job Summary

Aprio is seeking a Senior Security Analyst to monitor, triage, and respond to threats across our managed security clients using the Microsoft security stack. You will serve as the first line of defense for dozens of client environments, working primarily in Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR to detect, investigate, and contain threats before they cause harm. This role will carry a share of after-hours and on-call coverage to ensure clients are protected around the clock. Our Sentinel SOAR platform automates enrichment and first-response containment, allowing you to focus on investigation and judgment — not copy-paste triage.
You will deliver clear, client-ready incident communication and contribute to the continuous improvement of detection and automation capabilities across a growing managed security practice.

What You'll Gain / Impact:

  • Opportunity to protect dozens of client environments across a variety of industries using enterprise-grade Microsoft security tools.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel SOAR automation, including Logic Apps playbooks and multi-tenant management.
  • Exposure to a structured, process-driven SOC with defined escalation paths, client runbooks, and direct client engagement.
  • Ability to contribute directly to detection engineering, automation development, and continuous improvement of managed security services.
  • Career growth within a high-performing managed security team at a nationally recognized professional services firm.

Key Responsibilities:

Monitoring and Triage
  • Monitor alerts and incidents across client tenants in Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365, and Defender for Cloud Apps.
  • Triage incidents enriched by automated playbooks, verify enrichment accuracy, and meet SLAs for acknowledgment. (MTTA) and containment (MTTC); differentiate true positives from false positives and benign activity.
  • Investigate suspicious sign-ins, risky users, and conditional access failures in Microsoft Entra ID.
Investigation and Response
  • Write and tune KQL queries for threat hunting, investigation, and detection rule development.
  • Trigger, approve, or reverse automated and on-demand containment playbooks in alignment with each client's authorized-actions matrix.
  • Operate and author Sentinel automation rules and Logic Apps playbooks.
  • Escalate confirmed incidents to senior analysts or incident response teams with a complete timeline and supporting evidence.
  • Review and approve or reject automated containment actions requiring human decision prior to execution — including isolating a device, disabling an account, or quarantining email for VIPs or critical assets.
  • Validate automated outcomes and reverse actions when incorrect, including releasing a device, re-enabling a user, or restoring email.
  • Monitor playbook health including Logic App run history, failed runs, throttling, and expired connector or API connections.
  • Maintain per-client automation settings including watchlists (VIPs, break-glass accounts, approved admin IPs, exempt hosts), automation rule order and conditions, and severity-based notification routing.
  • Ensure client notifications accurately reflect automated actions, including which action was taken, when, and which playbook executed.
  • Identify and report opportunities for new automation and tuning based on repeated manual steps, false-positive patterns, or noisy rules.
  • Follow change control procedures for automation; all changes to production playbooks are submitted through Sentinel Repositories/CI-CD — no direct edits to production environments.
Client Communication
  • Notify clients of incidents via phone, email, or ticketing system according to severity level and each client's runbook.
  • Write clear incident summaries and remediation recommendations tailored to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Contribute to monthly client security reports and service reviews.
Continuous Improvement
  • Tune analytics rules to reduce alert noise across multi-tenant environments.
  • Update runbooks, knowledge base articles, and shift handover notes.
  • Track emerging threats and Microsoft security updates and share relevant findings with the team.
Schedule and After-Hours Coverage
  • Participate in rotating after-hours, evening, weekend, and holiday on-call coverage to ensure 24/7 client protection.
  • Follow each client's escalation matrix, including after-hours phone contacts for critical incidents.
  • Maintain a reliable home internet connection and phone for remote shifts and on-call coverage.

Candidate Qualifications:

  • 3–4 years of experience in a SOC, MSSP, MDR, or IT security operations role.
  • Hands-on production experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR.
  • Working knowledge of KQL.
  • Solid understanding of Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Windows endpoints, networking fundamentals, and common attack techniques (MITRE ATT&CK).
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including composure and clarity during active client incidents.
  • Availability and willingness to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and on-call rotations.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Working knowledge of Sentinel automation rules, incident tasks, and playbook triggers (incident, alert, and entity triggers).
  • Sound judgment regarding when automation should be trusted and when it should be overridden.
  • Microsoft SC-200 certification required, plus at least one of the following (or committed to earning within 90 days of hire): SC-300, AZ-500, AZ-104, or SC-401.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience managing multiple tenants simultaneously through Azure Lighthouse or Defender XDR multi-tenant management.
  • Experience building Sentinel automation with Logic Apps, along with PowerShell or Python scripting.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Security Copilot, Defender for Cloud, and Microsoft Purview.
  • SC-401 (Information Security Administrator) or SC-100 (Cybersecurity Architect Expert).
  • Vendor-neutral certifications such as CISSP.
  • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, IT, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

title: Sr. Staff Engineer, GNC (R6391)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

You will build and lead the Guidance & Control (G&C) team for Ranger, a fully autonomous aircraft designed for conventional runway takeoff and landing. You will own the team’s technical direction, development roadmap, and project execution, delivering flight control and flight-autonomy capabilities from requirements and architecture through flight verification.

What You'll Do

  • Build and lead the Ranger G&C team. Define staffing needs, establish clear technical ownership, and develop the team through mentorship, design reviews, and hands-on problem solving.
  • Own the G&C development roadmap. Translate program objectives into a phased plan for requirements development, algorithm maturation, simulation capabilities, software integration, verification, and flight testing. Establish measurable milestones and align priorities with program leadership and partner teams.
  • Own project execution and delivery. Scope and estimate work, allocate resources, manage schedules and cross-team dependencies, and track progress against deliverables. Identify technical and schedule risks early, drive mitigation plans, and communicate trade-offs and resource needs.
  • Define and deliver the G&C architecture, including Auto-Taxi and ATOL algorithms, inner- and outer-loop control laws, guidance, trajectory validation, flight-mode logic, and control allocation. Maintain stable, predictable aircraft performance through actuator constraints, disturbances, uncertainty, and defined degraded conditions.
  • Lead integration between flight autonomy and mission autonomy through A-GRA-aligned interfaces. Establish clear responsibilities for mission-level decision-making and vehicle-level execution, including command validation, flight-mode transitions, status reporting, and contingency coordination.
  • Lead development and validation of high-fidelity 6DOF simulation capabilities. Establish model fidelity requirements, validation plans, and uncertainty bounds to support control development, vehicle-level trades, and credible pre-flight performance predictions.
  • Own the G&C verification strategy and supporting compliance evidence. Define requirements-based acceptance criteria and verification coverage across linear and nonlinear analysis, Monte Carlo campaigns, sensitivity and failure studies, and software- and hardware-in-the-loop testing.
  • Drive cross-disciplinary trades with propulsion, aerodynamics, actuation, state estimation, embedded software, and autonomy teams. Translate G&C performance needs into subsystem requirements and resolve interface, timing, and integration issues.
  • Lead G&C preparation and analysis for ground and flight testing, including test-point selection, envelope-expansion planning, pre-flight predictions, and post-flight reconstruction. Provide evidence-based flight-readiness recommendations, resolve simulation-to-test discrepancies, and drive verified corrective changes.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in flight controls, GNC, or autonomous aircraft development, with demonstrated technical ownership of flight-vehicle systems from requirements and design through integration and flight test.
  • Experience building or leading engineering teams, including establishing technical direction, assigning ownership, mentoring engineers, and delivering complex development efforts through coordinated team execution.
  • Demonstrated ownership of technical roadmaps and project execution, including work scoping, effort estimation, staffing plans, milestone definition, dependency management, and technical risk reduction.
  • Deep expertise in aircraft flight dynamics, classical and modern control theory, nonlinear systems, and fixed-wing control law design, including stability, performance, and robustness across the operating envelope.
  • Strong experience developing or validating high-fidelity 6DOF simulations and using ground- and flight-test data to identify modeling limitations, characterize uncertainty, and improve predictive capability.
  • Experience defining and executing requirements-based verification strategies, including linear and nonlinear analysis, Monte Carlo studies, integrated testing, and flight-test analysis.
  • Experience integrating guidance, control, and flight-mode logic, with a clear understanding of the division between flight autonomy and mission autonomy and the interfaces needed to support feasible vehicle-level execution.
  • Proficiency in C++, with experience implementing, reviewing, and debugging G&C or simulation software and addressing real-time execution constraints. Experience using MATLAB and/or Python for engineering analysis and verification.
  • Strong technical judgment and communication skills, with the ability to resolve ambiguous, cross-disciplinary problems and clearly communicate decisions, assumptions, risks, and limitations to engineers and program leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading development, integration, or flight verification of autonomous fixed-wing aircraft.
  • Direct experience defining, implementing, or verifying A-GRA-aligned interfaces, or integrating flight autonomy with a separate mission-autonomy provider.
  • Experience building a G&C team or development capability for a new aircraft program, including establishing technical practices, simulation infrastructure, verification workflows, and development plans.
  • Experience applying flight safety and airworthiness processes, deriving flight control requirements, and producing supporting artifacts such as simulation descriptions, verification reports, and flying-qualities analyses.
  • Experience evaluating navigation errors, air data uncertainty, altitude-sensing limitations, latency, and data validity against flight control and ATOL performance requirements.
  • Experience establishing software- and hardware-in-the-loop capabilities, automated regression testing, and CI/CD workflows using Linux, Git, and modern C++ development practices.
  • Experience integrating steady-state or transient NPSS propulsion models or model outputs into a 6DOF simulation environment.
  • Experience leading G&C execution in developmental flight-test programs, balancing rapid iteration with configuration control, verification rigor, and disciplined flight-readiness assessments.

title: Founding GTM
location: New York, NY / Los Angeles, CA / Denver, CO
description:
Company

The earth beneath our feet holds extraordinary, untapped capacity to accelerate the clean energy transition, with limitless geo-energy available under every real estate asset. Bedrock Energy is on a mission to transform the heating and cooling of buildings, using carbon-free, hyper-efficient, and ultra-safe geothermal energy to radically reduce costs for people and the environment. Incorporated in 2022, Bedrock has raised over $25M in capital and brings together exceptional talent to scale up geothermal heating/cooling for real estate and infrastructure developers in any city in the world. We seek creative, collaborative, proactive team members who inspire us with their high standards of excellence, integrity, and commitment to our shared mission.

Role

This role will be Bedrock's first commercial team member, shaping how we find, win, and grow our early customers. The role will start by working closely with the CEO, but within the first few months, will become the right hand to our incoming VP of Commercial, building out the sales org from the ground up. As the team grows, this role can grow with it, whether to direct a market segment or a team within the broader commercial function. At its best, this role will drive success across go-to-market strategy, sales deal delivery, functional systems, and commercially-critical special projects.

This is not a scripted BDR or SDR role. We're still sharpening our story and our product-market fit, so this role will simultaneously educate and learn from real customers, then systematize those learnings into a robust sales motion, with all the relevant back-end tools and collateral. You'll pitch, run deals, negotiate terms, and build the financial models that show customers (and the Bedrock team) why, when, and how a deal makes the most sense. You should have wide-ranging curiosity that spans from technical to economic to relational: that means quick uptake on building energy & HVAC concepts, DER economics and utility tariffs, real estate development & construction processes, geo-physics and drilling conditions, and interpersonal dynamics in customer organizations.

Responsibilities

Find and win early customers

  • Own deals end-to-end: prospecting, discovery, pitching, proposals, and close

  • Pitch and educate different buyer types across different deal types, from technical evaluators to executives, adapting the story to each

  • Run discovery on customer pain points, budget, and buying process, and build economic models and proposals to meet customer needs

  • Build economic models for customers (ROI, payback, cost savings) and Bedrock (pricing, margin, returns)

  • Draft term sheets and proposals, and negotiate contracts together with leadership and counsel

Shape the strategy and the story

  • Refine positioning, messaging, and pitch materials based on customer conversations

  • Spot patterns across customer and project models, and propose prioritization of segments, use cases, and channels

  • Turn customer feedback into clear input for product and leadership decisions

Build the sales engine

  • Mature our BD/sales funnel: stages, qualification criteria, handoffs, and metrics

  • Set up and maintain the CRM, pipeline reporting, and forecasting basics

  • Document what works into playbooks that future sales hires can pick up

  • Partner with CEO and VP of Commercial to structure and build the Sales org

Qualifications

  • 5-10 years of experience in roles that combine structured, analytical problem solving with customer-facing work, such as corporate development or strategy consulting

  • At least 2 years of hands-on BD or sales experience, ideally at an early-stage company

  • Strong analytical skills: comfortable building financial models in Excel or Sheets and explaining them simply to a customer or an internal partner

  • Clear, persuasive communication, in writing and in the room, with nimble adaptation to different audiences

  • Experience negotiating commercial structure, or a strong appetite to learn it quickly

  • Thrives in ambiguity: you can set your own priorities, build structure where none exists, and change course when the evidence says so

  • Low ego and high ownership: equally happy to update the CRM, write a contract redline, or present to a CEO

  • Travel of 25-50% in many months, including time at conferences or on job sites.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling into real estate and/or selling distributed energy

  • Familiarity with complex or multi-stakeholder sales cycles (e.g., enterprise, infrastructure, or project-based deals)

  • Background helping launch a new product, business line, or venture from zero to first revenue

Qualities

  • Proactivity: You take ownership, offer hypotheses, and hold yourself accountable.

  • Coachability: You welcome & react constructively to feedback and seek new skills with gusto.

  • Excellence: You hold yourself, and your team members, to high standards of performance.

  • Creativity: You enjoy finding resourceful, unconventional, flexible solutions to problems.

  • Integrity: You take pride in ethical, honest behavior, no matter who is around to see it.

  • Compassion: You remember empathy, respect, and care in your interactions with others.

  • Commitment to Diversity: You actively look to surround yourself & collaborate inclusively with people who are different from you in experience, background, worldview, and resources.

Bedrock Energy is building a strong culture based on our Organizational Values. In addition, we are committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Bedrock Energy is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

Homer Electric Association (HEA) is a member-owned electric utility serving the central and southern areas of the Kenai Peninsula in Alaska! We are excited to be seeking a Chief Technology Officer to join our executive team at our Homer or Kenai, Alaska, location.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Serve as the cooperative's Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Senior Manager under the Alaska Railbelt CIP (AK-CIP) standards, with overall authority for implementing and maintaining compliance.

  • Serve as liaison with regulatory authorities, and partner with the Board of Directors, executive team, and outside agencies on cybersecurity and technology strategy.

What makes you a good fit:

  • A bachelor's degree in information technology, engineering, business administration, or a related field.
  • Ten (10) years of business/industry experience, including at least five (5) years in IT security and three (3) years of supervisory experience.
  • Knowledge of NERC and Alaska Railbelt CIP requirements, communications, generating plant controls, and SCADA systems is preferred; utility industry experience is desired.
  • Current knowledge of cybersecurity laws, regulations, and frameworks such as NERC-CIP, AK-CIP, PCI-DSS, NIST SP 800-171, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
  • Ability to travel frequently, including by commercial and small aircraft and occasionally by boat.

Our R&D teams are responsible for application, evaluation and development of cutting-edge technologies in a variety of agriculture and specialty markets. Helena is also developing and implementing the use of precision ag tools, such as drones and imagery for research and development purposes.

Within your territory, you will work with a variety of crops making applications of crop protection (herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, nematicides) and crop production (fertilizers, bioscience, biologicals) products. This includes working with various seeds and crops for new trait development, tolerance to pesticides for nutrient use, efficiency and drought stress tolerance.

You will collaborate with Helena teams and customers to present the findings of studies being conducted. In addition to your own responsibilities, you will also manage a team consisting of R&D Technicians and Interns. This role also gives you the opportunity to interface with cross-functional Helena teams in our Western Business Unit, as well as major ag industry manufacturers in crop production and crop protection industries.

WHAT YOUR DAY WILL LOOK LIKE

  • Facilitates the development protocols for product testing. This includes all aspects of the trial protocol such as cropping system, target and secondary pest, treatment list, application, evaluation parameters and trial location.
  • Negotiates and monitors all contracted research with cooperators within assigned area.
  • Assists in the construction, implementation, maintenance and dismantling of field and greenhouse research trials.
  • Orchestrates team schedule by communicating with growers, customers and employees.
  • Easily pivots to make changes based on needs.
  • Calculates, mixes and applies experimental and standard agricultural products in research and commercial applications.
  • Coordinates and stewards the collection, packaging and shipping of all products used in R&D within assigned area.
  • Prepares and coordinates local and state regulatory compliance documentation.
  • Monitors trials, analyzes and compares data and documents results with film, video, notes, etc.
  • Enters application and evaluation data into our statistical analysis research programs.
  • Analyzes trial data and prepares reports and presentations for distribution.
  • Provides research results to appropriate team members, vendors, academia and customers including sales meeting presentations, training and supplier meetings.
  • Notes product handling, mixing and application characteristics and makes suggestions for improvement.
  • Develops and implements methods and procedures for monitoring products/projects. This includes providing information to support budgets, expenditures, data and progress reports.
  • Instructs and leads Helena R&D Interns and Technicians.
  • Performs facility and equipment inspections and maintenance.
  • May be required to operate a company vehicle.
  • Provides excellent customer service to all internal and external customers.
  • Other work-related duties as assigned by your leader.
  • Regular and reliable attendance is required.
  • Follows all company policies and procedures.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in Science is preferred.
  • Three years of agricultural field research experience is required.
  • Prior leadership experience is preferred.
  • Qualified Applicator License (QAL) is required but can be gained during employment.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Presentation skills.
  • Project management skills.
  • Ability to influence others without directly managing them.
  • Time management.
  • Ability to easily adapt to unexpected changes in project scope.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate a high level of activity under a variety of conditions and constraints.
  • Interpersonal skills.
  • Organizational skills.
  • Data analysis skills.
  • Proficient computer skills (Microsoft Office, research software, internet, etc.).
  • Ability to read, write and speak in English is required.
  • Communicating in Spanish is a valuable skill at Helena.
  • Valid U.S. driver's license is required and must meet all company requirements to drive a Helena vehicle.

Successful completion of a drug test and background check is required for all positions at Helena.

BEING A LEADER AT HELENA

At Helena, our leaders are expected to demonstrate the same qualities that we value in our employees -- integrity, passion and accountability. In this leadership role, you will be responsible for overseeing other team members. This includes carrying out leadership responsibilities such as interviewing, hiring, training and coaching employees; planning, assigning and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees and addressing complaints and resolving problems by following all of Helena's policies, procedures and applicable laws.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL ASPECTS OF THE JOB

At Helena, safety is our highest priority. We seek out extensive safety measures and put them in place to minimize exposure to anything that could be potentially harmful to our employees.

The work environment for this position will be in an office setting and outdoors in all types of weather conditions with exposure to outdoor elements. When working outdoors and possibly around moving equipment/mechanical parts, you could be exposed to fumes, airborne particles, chemical and biological hazards, vibrations and a risk of electrical shock.

This position requires you to use your hands for many different tasks and to talk, hear, walk, stand sit, stand (8 hours a day or more), lifting, carrying, pushing or pulling (up to and including 50lbs or more), reaching overhead (up to and including 25lbs), climbing, gripping, grasping and twisting using hands and wrists, bending and stooping for long periods of time, working below knee levels for short periods of time and working above shoulder level for short periods.

BENEFITS AT HELENA

  • Helena's robust 401(k) Savings Plan offers you a 100% company-match up to 5% starting on your first day. As your years of service with Helena increase, so does our company-match - up to 10% based on your contribution amount.
  • Three-year vesting on company-match with 1,000 hours of service.
  • Access your earned pay between paydays through Earned Wage Access (EWA) with DailyPay.
  • Employees are eligible for paid time-off and holiday pay.
  • This position is eligible for overtime pay.
  • Free Term Life Insurance at 1x your annual base pay - paid for by Helena at no cost to you.
  • Free Short & Long-Term Disability.
  • Up to four weeks of paid Parental Leave.
  • Education Assistance.
  • And much more!

For more detailed information about our benefits, visit helenacareers.com/benefits.

title: Senior Rendering Engineer (UE5)
description:
Who is SkyBox Labs?
Recognized as one of BC's Top Employers (2025), SkyBox Labs is a game development studio that works on some of the world’s most iconic games. The studio is currently working on projects in the Minecraft universe, supporting the dev team at Bungie on Destiny 2, supporting development of Fallout 76, in addition to work on unannounced IP. Since our inception in 2011, SkyBox Labs has evolved from a small team of eight individuals to a fully established team of Engineers, Artists, Animators, Designers, Producers, and more. Come join our hybrid team in our Burnaby, BC studio today!
PLEASE NOTE: At this time, we are only able to hire candidates who are legally eligible to work in Canada and reside within Canada.

Interested? Let’s talk about what we’re hiring for:

SkyBox Labs is looking for a Senior Rendering Engineer to join our team on an ambitious AAA co-development project set within a highly anticipated universe.

Working in close collaboration with our partner studio, you’ll play a pivotal role at the intersection of rendering technologies and engine systems. As part of our specialized engineering group, you'll join dynamic cross-functional strike teams to tackle real-world runtime challenges, optimize low-level performance, and ensure our visual systems run cleanly under the hood.

Using UE5’s toolset and your own technical chops, you'll navigate complex engine architecture to keep graphics pipelines smooth and performant. This role is built for proactive problem solvers: you'll thrive here if you enjoy taking high-level technical goals, digging into large codebases, asking the right questions, and driving practical solutions forward across both graphics and core engine terrain.

This team works in a hybrid capacity, with three days a week at our studio in Burnaby, BC.

A snapshot of your role:

  • Cross-Discipline & Co-Dev Collaboration: Partner closely with feature strike teams and engineering leads—both internally and with our partner studio—to support rendering needs, clear technical blockers, and keep visual feature workflows moving.
  • Large-Engine Debugging: Investigate complex issues within the Unreal Engine frame—taking captures, tracking down elusive bugs, and diagnosing low-level code across a massive, evolving codebase.
  • Performance & Memory Optimization: Drive crucial profiling, memory management, and runtime optimization passes across graphics and engine subsystems to hit key performance targets.
  • UE5 Rendering Support: Maintain, debug, and implement best practices across core Unreal rendering features, including Lumen, Megalights, Nanite, Niagara, Substrate, Virtual Textures, and Virtual Shadow Maps.
  • Proactive Problem-Solving & Communication: Navigate high-level technical goals and open-ended requests with autonomy—taking ownership to investigate complex problems, communicate proactively across disciplines, and deliver solid results.

Sound like you? This is what we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of experience in real-time graphics and/or systems programming roles touching on graphics, preferably in the games industry.
  • Strong C++ Foundations: Deep expertise in C++ with a balanced understanding of core engine systems and rendering pipelines.
  • Unreal Engine 5 Experience: Hands-on experience working with UE5 and a practical understanding of its core rendering technologies (e.g. Lumen, Megalights, Nanite, Niagara, Substrate, RVTs, SVTs, and VSMs ).
  • Debugging & Profiling Mastery: Proven track record hunting down elusive bugs and profiling performance in large codebases using standard tools (such as RenderDoc, Pix, Unreal Insights, or NSight).
  • Self-Motivated & Autonomous Mindset: Comfort operating in an environment where solutions aren't always pre-defined. You enjoy rolling up your sleeves, taking broad objectives, and figuring out the answers proactively.
  • Collaborative Communication: Strong teamwork skills and the adaptability to work effectively within a co-development environment across disciplines and partner studios.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Console Development Experience: Experience shipping or developing real-time applications/games on modern console hardware (PS5, Xbox Series X|S).
  • Shader & Material Optimization: Strong background in HLSL/GLSL, custom shader development, or optimizing complex technical art materials and shaders for runtime performance.

And here is why we think you'll love working at SkyBox:

  • Annual bonus and up to 3% RRSP matching available
  • Comprehensive health benefits, along with a supportive Maternity and Parental Leave policy
  • Flexible hybrid working arrangements: leverage our beautiful studio spaces as needed and have the ability to work from home on certain projects
  • Take care of your mental health with our Employee Assistance Program, 3 weeks of vacation leave, and our free gym at our Burnaby Studio
  • We relentlessly support your growth and development! Level up your C++ skills at SkyBox University, explore other disciplines through our Guild Program, and expand your game dev knowledge with Lunch & Learns. You’ll join a culture of empowerment, collaboration, and personal growth.
  • Social events! Have fun with the team at trivia nights, karaoke nights, movie nights, and various group activities. Join our soccer team, game jams, or a board game sesh after work. You name it, we’ve got it!
  • Get involved with our diverse community through Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that champion Diversity, Equity & Inclusion initiatives and promote a supportive environment
  • You’ll contribute to industry-leading titles!
The base salary range for this position is $125,000 to $170,000. The stated pay scale reflects the range that SkyBox Labs reasonably expects to pay for this position. Your base salary and level will be determined by various factors including, but not limited to, qualifications, skills, experience, and demonstrated competencies.

Our commitment to you:
SkyBox Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to developing and maintaining a diverse workforce. You’ll join a collaborative, inclusive culture where we succeed together, and like-minded people work naturally together to achieve great things (and games!).
Only candidates who reside in Canada or are willing to relocate will be considered for this role. Additionally, although we appreciate all interest, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Systems Test Engineer
description:
Autonomous vehicles have some of the largest, most complex software ever shipped in a safety-critical environment. Solving that problem is one of the most exciting technical challenges of our lifetime.

As a Systems Test Engineer on our System Behavior Analysis Autonomous team, you will play a critical role in the development of Zoox's autonomous platform, working with a broad set of engineering teams across Zoox. You will help triage and root cause the issues identified during testing and real-world operations. You will also produce reports and insights that inform leadership on the overall quality and influence of engineering decisions. Your ability to distill complex systems, root cause issues and articulate risk to the business will be crucial to producing a safe and stable vehicle platform.

In this role, you will:

  • Utilize data analytics to analyze and diagnose a wide range of system faults and errors related to hardware, software, and sensor data from both on-road testing and system simulation runs.
  • Effectively categorize and prioritize issues based on severity, priority, and potential impact on safety and performance by working collaboratively with cross-functional teams (engineering, software, testing) and offshore teams.
  • Identify trends in system failures and propose preventative measures to improve overall system safety and robustness by producing clear and concise reports of system issues, troubleshooting steps, and root cause analysis.
  • Work to define and report on the operational characteristics of SBA execution including cost and capacity forecasting.
  • Be hands-on, lead by example, and develop tools and workflows to drive improvements for both quality and quantity aspects of the triage operations.
  • Demonstrate operational agility by quickly adapting to changing priorities, managing multiple tasks simultaneously, and implementing effective solutions in dynamic environments.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or STEM-related field
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in systems troubleshooting and diagnostics, preferably in the automotive or embedded systems industry
  • Experience with Git, Agile methodologies, and scripting/programming languages (preferably Python)
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a methodical approach to root cause analysis
  • A passion for autonomous vehicle technology and safety is essential

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience in a Quality Assurance or Triage role for Autonomous Driving
  • Project Management experience on programs involving cross-functional partners and offshore teams
  • Experience with Change Management, Analytics, or Simulation tools
About Zoox
Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

title: AI Enablement Strategist
description:
Summary: The AI Enablement Strategist is responsible for accelerating HODGE’s adoption of artificial intelligence and process automation as enterprise capabilities. The role serves as a central lead for discovery, prioritization, governance, and cultural adoption of AI across enterprise functions - Accounting, Finance, HR, IT, Operational Excellence, Marketing, and Training. The position does not build production solutions; it ensures the right problems are identified, prioritized, governed, and handed off to IT, Operational Excellence, or functional teams for delivery, while remaining accountable for outcomes. The role staffs the AI Steering Committee, chairs the AI Champion Group, and partners across departments to coach leaders and teams on responsible AI usage, measure business impact, and build durable enterprise AI literacy. This role works with a high degree of visibility and cross-functional collaboration working directly with executive leadership and Directors across the enterprise.


Essential Duties: Essential job duties for this position include the following items.

AI Enablement & Cultural Stewardship: Coach leaders and teams on responsible AI use and effective prompting practices. Build enterprise AI literacy that supports and enhances human judgment. Reinforce departmental ownership of processes and protect HODGE culture through the AI transition.

Champion Group Leadership: Revive and chair the AI Champion Group as the network for use-case piloting and cultural adoption. Refresh membership, establish charter, set cadence, and maintain a healthy use-case backlog.

Steering Committee Staffing: Staff the AI Steering Committee with intake, prioritization recommendations, guardrail proposals, and impact reporting. Translate departmental opportunities into prioritization decisions the Committee can act on.

Process Discovery & Opportunity Identification: Sit with departments to observe, document, and map priority workflows. Distinguish manual improvements, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled opportunities. Quantify baseline effort, cycle time, quality, and cost impacts.

Prioritization & Handoff: Manage intake and prioritization of automation and AI initiatives. Route builds to IT, Operational Excellence, or business units based on defined guidelines. Coordinate cross-functional initiatives through a unified brief with a designated business owner.

Measurement & Communication: Standardize reporting on savings, cycle time, and quality improvements. Maintain the Wins repository and convert use cases into quantified ROI. Communicate wins and lessons learned Enterprise-wide.

Continuous Improvement: Conduct ninety-day post-implementation reviews for delivered initiatives. Maintain an iteration backlog alongside the new build backlog to support continuous improvement after go-live.

title: Statutory Financial Reporting Analyst
description:
1. Prepares the financial reporting requirements for the State of Hawaii Insurance Division (DCCA) in accordance with the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures manual:
    • Prepares the "Annual Statement" for the Association and ensure timely filing of all required reports. Applies thorough knowledge of Statutory Accounting Principles (SAP). Maintains PC-based software to prepare reports and resolve any validation errors. Remains current on legislation and accounting guidance related to SAP accounting rules and bring changes to accounting guidance to the attention of management and team.

title: Fiber Yard Operator
description:
General Summary
The Fiber Yard Operator is responsible for staging the bailed and loose raw materials for the paper mill. They will be operating intermittently Fork-Lifts, Front End Loaders, and/or Bobcat mobile equipment in a 24/7 operation working 12 hour shifts in a 4 shift rotational concept. They must be able to get on & off equipment regularly, understand inventory procedures, some basic computer skills, and be able to communicate clearly with the team and their supervisor. They must be able to read orders, possess basic mathematical skills, complete documentation, and be able to operate various types of small to medium sized industrial mobile equipment.

Essential Job Functions
1) Mental Ability – The Fiber Yard Operator must be able to read orders and prepare reports legibly and properly. They must be able to communicate orally with all personnel in the plant. They must be able to operate a calculator for basic mathematical computations. Basic typing skills are essential for basic computer use and/or computerized scanning machine.

2) Physical Ability – The Fiber Yard Operator must be able to climb up onto various types of industrial equipment truck and be able to operate steering controls, hand levers, and/or two foot pedals. There could be occasional climbing up a ladder. They must have excellent depth perception to maneuver the equipment and raw materials around crowded areas with co-workers nearby. Must be able to frequently get on and off equipment and the use of hand tools, specifically cutting pliers, is required.

3) Safety – It is plant policy to work in a safe manner. All Fiber Yard Operators must ensure guards are in place, follow lock-tag-try procedures, observe hazards such as nip points, and follow plant and department safety rules.

Physical Demands
Work is light difficulty, fast paced, physically demanding, and will be outside. Fiber Yard Operators must be able to operate a steering wheel, hydraulic levers, foot pedals, and a handheld scanner. They must be able to observe their immediate area for safe operation of mobile industrial equipment in crowded areas. Occasionally, they may be asked to maneuver items by hand and be able to lift up to 50lbs.

Education and/or Experience
1) Post-secondary educational degree (2 to 4 year degree from college, university, technical-school, military, vocational or other advanced educational institution) is highly preferred.

Additional Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Requirements
1) Drug testing/Screening, Background Checks, Physical exam, and Reference Checks

title: Director, Development - Texas
description:
Director, Development

College Possible- Texas

This Work Is Our Mission

At College Possible, we believe talent is universal. For many students, the path to college can feel overwhelming or out of reach. That's where you come in.

We support students on their journey to higher education by providing personalized coaching, resources, and guidance. When you join College Possible, you become part of a team dedicated to making college access and success a reality. Together, we help students navigate the admissions process, overcome challenges, and earn their degrees.

Our Impact

87% of College Possible students are admitted to college and are enrolled at 866 colleges and universities across the United States. Nationwide, we've served 99,000+ students since 2000.

Why Join Our Team?

When you work at College Possible, you're not just taking a job-you're advancing a mission to help more students get to and through college. You'll play a direct role in helping students achieve their educational goals and build brighter futures.

Key Benefits

  • Professional Growth Access training, mentorship, and career development opportunities as you support student success.
  • Mission-Driven Impact Make a direct difference in students' lives by helping them access and complete college.
  • Collaborative Community Join a team that values teamwork, innovation, and excellence in service of students.
  • Work-Life Balance Enjoy flexible work options, unlimited PTO, and resources to support your well-being.

Your Role as Development Director

The Director of Development leads College Possible Texas's fundraising department, securing philanthropic investment that helps students from low-income backgrounds access and complete college. The director personally manages the design and implementation of the CP Texas marketing and communications plan, priority donor and funder relationships, builds a growing individual-giving pipeline, and leads the annual fundraising plan across individual, foundation, and corporate support. Working closely with Texas leadership, the Advisory Board, and national advancement colleagues, the director strengthens renewals, develops new funding opportunities, and maintains clear revenue forecasts and timely stewardship. This role combines strategic leadership with direct fundraising execution statewide across Texas.

Major Gifts: Act as primary manager to identify, cultivate and play a lead role in soliciting and closing major gifts from foundations, corporations, and high net worth individuals that generate five figure gifts and above.

Strategic Planning and Analysis: Develop and execute an annual fundraising plan, to include revenue forecasts, financial modeling, donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies to meet and exceed annual fundraising targets. Analyze local data and monthly reports across all strategic outreach efforts and campaigns to critically assess effectiveness and progress towards goals. Responsible for analyzing and monitoring program data being reported to board and donors.

Grant and Appeal Writing: Develop, write, and submit grant proposals, direct mail, and digital appeal campaigns to support the achievement of CP Texas annual revenue goals. Build proposal budgets and incorporate financial modeling and forecasting techniques that support grant proposals. Use the Salesforce database and internal tracking practices to record application and reporting deadlines to ensure timely submission and compliance.

Prospecting and Cultivation: Lead prospecting and donor research to cultivate high-net-worth individuals and secure institutional support. Implement strategies to inspire prospective supporters to become donors and increase the number of donors to the annual operating fund.

Fundraising Events: Plan and implement events and activities (volunteer experiences, tours, receptions, friend-raisers, etc.) for individual major gift donors, using existing activities as appropriate. Engage in networking activities or other opportunities to generate potential donor prospects for cultivation.

Relationship Management and Stewardship: Track and report relationship management activity using Salesforce CRM system, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, proposal submission, and stewardship of prospective and current funders. Monitor weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual activity to achieve individual performance measures (e.g. meetings, proposals, major gift revenue) through a strong stewardship strategy.

Communications/Marketing: Lead the communications, marketing, and public relations efforts for College Possible Texas and work closely with the National Communications Team. Oversee heads-up marketing efforts- quarterly newsletter, social media, marketing slide deck and website maintenance. Manage the creation and production of printed and electronic newsletters and press releases, and guide media relations and social media strategies.

Site Leadership: The Development Director plays a critical role as a leader at the Texas site. They will represent College Possible externally within the business, academic and philanthropic communities. They will build a strong culture of collaboration, excellence, and strong strategic leadership.

Other duties as assigned or required

What You Bring

Education/Certifications/Licenses:

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • Master's degree and/or CFRE preferred

Related Work Experience:

  • Six or more years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, or equivalent demonstrated achievement
  • A minimum three years of supervisory experience

Position Qualifications:

  • Must possess strong written, oral and presentation communication skills, have substantial experience in developing clear and concise funding proposals, and the ability to explain program outcomes qualitatively and quantitatively
  • Must have a demonstrated ability to meet financial goals for major gift giving, with a proven track record of cultivating and securing five-figure gifts and above, and successful experience with prospect research, outreach and developing cultivation and solicitation strategies
  • Individual must be able to think strategically and creatively, and must have excellent interpersonal skills and a demonstrated record of completing assignments, multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, and working with minimal supervision
  • Effective partnership with executives and board members; staff or contractor supervision where the role requires it
  • Individual must possess a significant commitment to the mission of helping historically underserved students earn admission to college and persist toward degree completion
  • Experience with federal grant writing and compliance is a plus
  • Strong management abilities with significant supervisory experience

Computer/Software Skills:

  • Strong computer skills, including demonstrated proficiency in: Microsoft Word, Excel and donor database software
  • Salesforce experience preferred

Other Skills and Abilities:

  • Self-starter with the ability to prioritize multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously
  • Proven record of facilitating collaboration and cooperation with organizations and the community
  • Attention to detail, including proofreading and project follow-through
  • Comfort with data collection, analysis, and a strong focus on results

Physical Requirements:

  • Travel required up to 20% to meet face-to-face with key funders, represent the organization at high-profile events, and perform site visits to evaluate project impact
  • This position primarily involves computer-based and administrative work in an office and/or remote work environment. The role requires regular use of a computer and participation in virtual and in-person meetings. Occasional movement of office, program, or event materials may be required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

What We Offer

In addition to joining a committed, diverse, values-based organization, we offer:

  • An opportunity for you to have a tremendous impact both internally and in the broader country
  • A work-from-home/hybrid environment with regular travel to meetings, events, and co-working opportunities

  • Excellent benefits including complete health, dental, life, short-term and long-term insurance

Responsibilities include training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; conflict resolution; team building; coaching and leading employees to improve; addressing complaints and resolving problems; documentation; and setting an example of superior behavior, attitude, and performance.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES -

  • Maintain quality, efficiency, and production levels set by management. Communicate these standards to your staff.
  • Report on quality concerns to Corrugator and Plant Superintendent. Assist in determining quality guidelines.
  • Establish high morale within your department by showing fairness, consistency, and an interest in employee problems. Maintain confidentiality.
  • Maintain inventories of roll stock and corrugator supplies.
  • Coordinate with Corrugator Superintendent and Maintenance Manager or Leadman on any repairs or preventive maintenance done in the department.
  • Keep upper management informed of problems or situations that may affect the performance of your department.
  • Conduct weekly Production/Safety meetings with departmental personnel.
  • Communicate with necessary supervision to avoid problems between shift changes.
  • Improve career skills by enrolling yourself in seminars, technical courses, and related college courses.
  • Implement, maintain, comply with, and support all company policies and procedures, safety programs, and good housekeeping.
  • Additional duties may be assigned by management.

LEADERSHIP ATTRIBUTES - The individual must possess the following:

  • Superior time management skills include the ability to manage multiple issues concurrently and the ability to lead an effective and efficient meeting.
  • Teaching skills to function effectively as a teacher for his personnel both in the technical and administrative parts of the position.
  • Excellent crisis manager who demonstrates that he/she has a high emotional control under adverse conditions and can lead his/her personnel to a successful resolution.
  • Excellent employee relations skills include being an active listener, understanding how to appraise personnel, applying both positive and corrective feedback, being able to resolve conflicts either involving the Supervisor directly or as a third party, understanding and demonstrating positive motivational skills including coaching and delegation techniques.
  • Demonstrated confidence includes providing a consistent leadership style with an acceptable level of professional assertiveness.

PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS - The performance of the Supervisor will be measured as follows:

  • Operating standards - the Supervisor will need to meet or exceed the Operating Standards in the areas of quality, cost, safety, customer satisfaction and productivity. Such standards will be set annually and communicated to the Supervisor.
  • Personal growth - while the company will provide the tools to assist the Supervisor to grow professionally the responsibility for moving forward lies with the individual. Each year there will be goals developed and agreed to by the Supervisor and his/her superior.
  • Employee relations - through observations the Supervisor will be evaluated regarding his/her skills and advancements in the areas of motivational techniques and results, positive and corrective/constructive feedback, subordinate development and creating a positive work environment.
  • Creativity - this will be evaluated by how active the Supervisor is in participating in advancing the business through new and innovative ideas.

TECHNICAL SKILLS - The individual must have a working knowledge of the following:

  • Equipment design and capabilities that can be translated into efficient operation. This also supports the Supervisor's role of teacher and trainer for his/her personnel.
  • Cost issues to make daily decisions that will reduce overall costs and will help the Supervisor find areas that require improvement.
  • Quality standards.
  • Regulatory requirements including but not limited to wage and hour requirements, environmental and waste minimization, company policies, and personnel requirements including OSHA, DEQ and EEO.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE -

  • Minimum high school diploma or GED required.
  • Two years prior supervisory experience.
  • Candidates are PREFERRED who offer the following:
  • Prior work experience in the corrugated industry

LANGUAGE SKILLS - Able to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or employees of organization.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS - Able to read a tape measure with speed and accuracy. Able to calculate figures and amounts such as percentages, measurement, volume and rate. Able to apply concepts of high school math.

REASONING ABILITY - Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or graphic form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS - May be required to maintain a current Lift Truck Operator License.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS - The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee is occasionally required to sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT - The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those employee encounters while performing the functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

title: Senior Staff Sensor Integration Engineer (R6392)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

We are seeking a Sensor Integration Engineer to support selection, characterization, calibration, and integration of multi-modal navigation and localization sensors for the X-BAT State Estimation team. This role operates at the intersection of software, electrical, and mechanical engineering, requiring the ability to work across disciplines and directly contribute to cross-functional engineering efforts.

What You'll Do

Sensor Selection, Integration & Characterization
  • Support sensor integration activities from specification through production
  • Develop and execute sensor characterization and calibration procedures for IMUs, GNSS receivers, cameras, and other navigation sensors
  • Contribute to sensor trade studies and selection processes
Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work closely with electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and software engineering teams on:Electrical interfaces, power distribution, and signal conditioning
  • Mounting solutions, alignment, and thermal/vibration considerations
  • Software interfaces, drivers, data acquisition, and calibration implementation
  • Participate in design reviews across EE/ME/SW disciplines, providing interdisciplinary perspective and coordination
Technical Contributions
  • Develop and execute test plans for sensor performance characterization and validation
  • Document sensor characteristics, trade studies, and integration requirements
  • Develop or modify calibration scripts and data processing tools
  • Support development of calibration procedures and tooling
  • Debug issues spanning hardware-firmware-software boundaries
  • Review and contribute to schematics, CAD models, and code as necessary

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications:

  • BS in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or related field
  • 1-4 years of relevant experience (new grads with strong cross-functional internship/project experience will be considered)
  • Demonstrated ability to work across at least two of: electrical, mechanical, software domains
Technical Skills
  • Understanding of sensor measurement principles and error sources
  • Ability to read and understand electrical schematics and/or mechanical drawings
  • Basic proficiency in scripting or programming for data analysis (Python, MATLAB, or similar)
  • Familiarity with sensor communication protocols (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, etc.)
  • Hands-on experience with lab equipment and sensor testing
Cross-Functional Aptitude
  • Comfortable learning and working outside primary discipline
  • Ability to communicate effectively with engineers from different backgrounds
  • Willingness to engage with hardware, firmware, and software aspects of sensor systems
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills across multiple domains

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with navigation or localization sensors (IMUs, GNSS, cameras, altimeters, etc.)
  • Exposure to sensor calibration or characterization activities
  • Familiarity with embedded systems or real-time software
  • Understanding of coordinate transformations or sensor fusion concepts
  • Experience with automated testing or data acquisition systems
  • Knowledge of aerospace environmental testing or standards
Work Environment:
  • Collaborative team environment working with EE, ME, and SW engineers
  • Hands-on lab work combined with analysis and documentation
  • Occasional travel for team and supplier coordination or testing support

With over 450+ locations nationwide and over 6,000 employees we rank among the top agricultural service companies in volume and sales of agricultural products and services.

The Blender Operator is responsible for unloading, loading and blending fertilizer.

WHAT YOUR DAY WILL LOOK LIKE

  • Maintains conveyor systems.

  • Maintains cleanliness in fertilizer storage and loadout areas.

title: Technical Product Manager (GenAI & Data) - Contract
description:
CompassX is a boutique business and technology consulting firm. We help Fortune 500 and high-growth clients deliver their most strategic initiatives, from enterprise transformations to digital and data-driven projects. With over 15 years of proven results, we’ve expanded across industries including financial services, pharmaceuticals, aerospace, consumer products, and quick service restaurants.

We are honored to be recognized as a three-time winner of Consulting Magazine’s Best Boutique Firms to Work For, and previously recognized as a “Best Place to Work” in Southern California and one of INC.’s 5000 fastest-growing private companies in the U.S.

We’re looking for a Technical Product Manager to join a high-visibility engagement with one of our clients. This isn’t just an advisory or requirements-gathering role. You’ll work alongside the client’s Data Management team to learn how product and data actually move, from a marketing request through to a live in-person experience. Then you’ll build the tools that take the friction out of it.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. On any given day, you might be shadowing a Data Manager, mapping a workflow, talking through a data model with an engineer, or opening an IDE to ship a working prototype. The strongest candidates are GenAI builders first, with enough product and process instinct to know what’s worth building.

What You'll Do

Discover and Redesign

  • Work alongside Data Managers to understand how the work really happens, across intake, product authoring, handoffs, validation and publishing

  • Map workflows, systems and dependencies, set baseline measures like time-per-task, and identify where the biggest gains are

  • Challenge legacy processes and propose redesigned workflows, working through the right stakeholders to get them adopted

Build

  • Decide whether a problem calls for process change, automation, an integration, a purpose-built app or AI, and then build it

  • Independently build lightweight production applications, APIs, integrations and automation, using AI-assisted development tools without losing engineering discipline

  • Get prototypes into users’ hands quickly, gather feedback and improve sprint by sprint

  • Partner with the client’s engineers on larger builds while staying accountable for the product, architecture and outcome

Apply AI Where It Earns Its Place

  • Extend an existing AI-based product authoring capability to support more product types

  • Build practical AI tools such as authoring assistants, validation and anomaly checks, and workflow agents, with the right controls for data quality and human review

  • Recognize when a deterministic solution or a process fix is the better answer

Shape the Data Foundation

  • Help define the domain model for product and experience data

  • Replace spreadsheet-based tracking with a structured, queryable system that downstream platforms can draw from through API

  • Make sure what you build is documented, maintainable, and ready to hand over

What You'll Bring

  • 8+ years across software development, solutions architecture, technical product management or similar, with a track record of building and shipping tools yourself
  • Hands-on experience building applications, APIs and integrations. You don’t need to be a career software engineer, but you do need to be able to build robust solutions on your own
  • Practical experience developing LLM applications or agentic workflows
  • Strong data modeling and SQL skills
  • Experience working directly with end users to map processes and drive adoption across teams
  • Consulting or client-facing experience is a plus
  • Experience with product, menu, catalog or master data (PIM/MDM) is a strong plus
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher (Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems) or equivalent demonstrable experience
Our consultants say CompassX is a place where they can truly find their own path. As part of a smaller firm, they see the impact of their work, have an identity, and know their voice matters. They value the freedom to take the reins of their careers, shape their client work, and maintain a direct line to leadership.

With CompassX’s focus on serving local Southern California clients, consultants not only build lasting relationships but also see the results of their work in the communities where they live.

At CompassX, you won’t just follow a path - you’ll create one.

Job Summary
The Surgical Technologist plays a critical role in ensuring optimal surgical outcomes by maintaining sterile environments, preparing operating rooms, and assisting in surgical procedures. Responsibilities include following meticulous sterile techniques and assembling necessary surgical instruments and supplies according to physician preference cards. This role involves inspecting all equipment for functionality, ensuring it meets the specific requirements for each procedure. title: Machine Feeder 3rd Shift
description:
SUMMARY

Responsible for all activities associated with helping operators on all presses including setup, operation, cleanup, and recommending improvements to operations.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Set-up slotting, feed, and die-cut sections on the machine accurately in accordance with proper setup techniques.

Ensure all bolts for cutting dies are in place and tightly secured.

Check anilox rolls for damage.

Assist operator in other duties.

Monitor board quality, including - loose liner, warp, dimensions, caliper, and any other defects. Report any quality problems to the operator and sort as necessary to keep the machine running.

Work at the pace set by the machine operator.

Cross-train on other machines as necessary.

Be willing to move up the line of progression to the operator regardless of shift.

Complete necessary reports in an accurate and timely manner.

Turn in maintenance work orders to supervision for needed repairs. Be proactive in the maintenance of equipment.

Comply with all company policies and procedures, including safety and maintaining good housekeeping.

Helps operators adhere to the production schedule. Makes recommendations for optimizing the schedule to meet cost, quality, and service goals. Reports any unusual scheduling issues to Supervisor.

Additional duties may be assigned by management.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or GED.

Candidates are PREFERRED who offer the following:

Prior work experience in the corrugated industry.

6 months’ experience as a Flexo Stacker.

6 months’ experience in the Press and Finishing Department.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

Able to read and follow instructions on factory masters.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Able to read a tape measure with speed and accuracy. Able to calculate figures and amounts such as percentages, measurement, volume, and rate. Able to apply concepts of high school math.

REASONING ABILITY

Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or graphic form. Ability to deal with problems involving one or more concrete variables in standardized situations.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

The individual must have a working knowledge of the following:

Equipment design and capabilities that can be translated into efficient operation.

Product layouts and production specifications

Product quality specifications

Quality standards

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

May be required to maintain a current Lift Truck Operator License.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee is occasionally required to sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS

The performance of the employee will be measured as follows:

Operating standards - the employee will need to meet or exceed the Operating Standards in the areas of quality, cost, safety, customer satisfaction, and productivity. Such standards will be set annually and communicated to the employee.

Personal growth - while the company will provide the tools to assist the employee to grow professionally the responsibility for moving forward lies with the individual. Each year there will be goals developed and agreed to by the employee and his/her superior.

Employee relations - through observations the employee will be evaluated regarding his/her behaviors associated with appropriate human interaction, respect, and communication.

Creativity - this will be evaluated by how active the employee is in participating in advancing the business through new and innovative ideas.

title: Maintenance Tech - 1st Shift
description:
Maintenance Tech – 1st Shift

Shift/Hours: Monday – Friday 7:00AM – 3:00PM

Starting Pay Rate: $27.00/hr + (pending experience)

As a Maintenance Technician at Pratt Industries – Tulsa, OK you will be a crucial part of our day to day. Our Maintenance Technicians maintain and repair the machinery and building involved in turning recycled paper into sheets of corrugated board and getting them to our customers! Think boxes for Domino’s Pizzas, moving with Home Depot, Amazon deliveries, Hello Fresh meals, and more! (And yes, we make those!) If you’re looking for a company that will invest in you as much as you invest in them, Pratt Industries is the place for you! We value your maintenance knowledge, skills, and experience by providing competitive pay, quick benefits, and unparalleled career growth opportunities.

Give and Get:

What You’ll Get:

  • Insurance Benefits and wellness reimbursement within one month
  • Paid holidays from day one and 401(k) with match at 3 months
  • Tuition reimbursement at one year
  • Excellent benefits package including medical, dental, short-term disability and HSA
  • Paid Childbearing/parental leave at one year
  • Healthy Lifestyle program with up to $1,200 awarded each year to your HSA
  • Employee Assistance Programs to help you manage your life at work and at home
  • Safety and PPE Reimbursements
  • Cell phone discount with 2 major providers
  • Monthly incentive bonus if plant goals are met

What You’ll Give:

  • A Commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement
  • Dedication to maintaining equipment and production area cleanliness
  • Leadership in training and assisting fellow team members, including machine operators and helpers.
  • Active participation in meeting production schedules and resolving challenges proactively

Key Duties and Success Factors

  • Safety & Compliance: Exercise safe work habits and maintain a clean and safe working area, follow all company safety policies and procedures, and ensure compliance with operational guidelines and OSHA regulations.
  • Quality Assurance: Maintain company standards for quality, and perform inspections and ensure all parts and assemblies meet production specifications.
  • Operational Efficiency: Install, maintain, and repair machinery and equipment in plants and related facilities, perform preventative maintenance on motors, die cutters, hydraulic systems, conveyors, steam systems, and other related plant equipment. Operate a variety of hand and power tools, equipment, and machinery in maintenance, repair, and fabrication of parts.
  • Technical Responsibilities: Interpret electrical and mechanical diagrams and drawings, mount electrical components such as drives, servos, PLCs, circuit breakers, transformers, and relays. Perform wiring, labeling, and testing of electrical components. Cut, strip, bend, and form wire cable and conduit used to connect circuits and sub-assemblies. Perform soldering, crimping, and securing of electrical components. And conduct functional and continuity tests using an ohmmeter, test lights, and other electrical testing instruments.
  • Training & Development: Cross-train in multiple technical areas to enhance skills, and participate in continued education and training opportunities.
  • Reporting & Maintenance: Accurately complete work orders and maintenance reports, and identify potential equipment failures and proactively recommend repairs.
  • Flexibility & Teamwork: Work flexible hours, including weekends and overtime as needed, assist in maintaining a clean and safe work environment, and support plant inspections and operational adjustments as needed.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

  • Experience: 2-5 years of experience within a manufacturing or maintenance environment, and preferred experience in the manufacturing industry (e.g., corrugated industry).
  • Machine Setup & Material Handling: Ability to install, maintain, and troubleshoot industrial machinery and equipment. Experience in handling electrical and mechanical components.
  • Quality Control & Production Monitoring: Familiarity with inspecting production processes and ensuring equipment reliability. Ability to interpret schematics, blueprints, and technical manuals.
  • Basic Troubleshooting: Ability to diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic issues. Proficiency in problem-solving and identifying system improvements.
  • Skills:
    • Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude
    • Ability to operate and maintain various hand and power tools
    • Knowledge of general maintenance principles and skilled trades applications
    • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow safety and operational procedures
    • Basic computer skills for tracking maintenance records and reports
    • Effective communication and teamwork abilities
    • Self-motivated with a history of good work performance and attendance
  • Physical Requirements: Regularly required to stand, walk, and work in physically demanding conditions, frequent use of hands for handling, reaching, and operating tools/machinery. Ability to lift and move up to 100 pounds occasionally, 50 pounds frequently, and 20 pounds constantly. Frequently climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, and reach.
  • Certifications: Preferred apprenticeship or associate degree in a relevant field. May be required to maintain a Lift Truck Operator License
  • Work Environment: Regular exposure to moving mechanical parts and high-noise environments, frequent exposure to wet and humid conditions. Occasional exposure to high places, airborne particles, and vibration. Fast-paced and safety-oriented work setting

If you are ready to take the next step in your career and join a company that values growth and teamwork, apply today and help us continue to make Pratt Industries a leader in the Corrugating industry!
